0.DSCR:
A super robot designed and developed by Dr. Juzo
Kabuto.
 It is completed when Kouji's Hover Pilder, launched
from a sewage treatment plant with the shout "Mazin
Go!", combines with the head (Pilder On).
 It runs on photon power, and boasts a jumping
ability of 20 meters, a grip strength of 150
tons, and 650,000 horsepower. Its armor,
covered in Chogokin Z, is extremely sturdy, and
ordinary attacks cannot leave so much as a scratch
on it.
 It carries a variety of weapons, including the
'Rocket Punch,' which fires its arms via rocket
propulsion, the 'Breast Fire,' which emits thermal
energy from its chest plate, and the 'Rust
Hurricane,' which blasts a powerful acid-laden wind
from its mouth. But its arsenal did not stop there
- Professor Yumi and his colleagues went on to add
new weapons and enhance its performance again and
again.
 Among its many upgrades, the most famous is the
episode in which it overcame its greatest weakness,
its inability to fly, thanks to the 'Jet Scrander'
flight-assist device. This sequence of 'gaining
wings and flying freely through the sky' embodies a
longing humanity has held since the age of myth, and
it left an extremely strong impression. As a
result, many robot anime since have followed in its
footsteps in one form or another.

1.DSCR:
A female-form robot developed by Professor Yumi to
serve as Mazinger Z's partner.
 It is the successor to the Aphrodite A, which was
destroyed in battle against a Mechanical Beast, and
it is completed when the large motorcycle 'Scarlet
Mobile,' piloted by Sayaka, combines with its head.
However, unlike the Aphrodite A, which was
originally built for resource mining, Diana A was
designed for combat from the outset, giving it
considerably improved combat capability by
comparison.
 With photon power as its energy source, Chogokin Z
armor, and a combining-type cockpit, it shares much
in common with Mazinger Z, making it a robot truly
worthy of the name 'partner.'

2.DSCR:
A super robot secretly designed and developed by
Dr. Kenzo Kabuto, based on Mazinger Z.
 Like Mazinger Z, it is completed when Tetsuya's
Brain Condor, launched from a whirlpool with the
shout "Mazin Go!", combines with the head (Fire
On).
 It runs on the same photon power as Mazinger Z, but
its armor, made of Chogokin New Z, surpasses
Chogokin Z and is even sturdier than Mazinger Z's.
 Owing to the circumstances of its development, many
of its weapons are enhanced or developed versions of
those found on Mazinger Z. Its unique attacks
include the 'Mazinger Blade,' a pair of giant swords
stored in its legs, and 'Thunder Break,' which
stores lightning as energy before unleashing it in a
strike.
 It also has the Scramble Dash flight device built
into its back, allowing it to fly at Mach 4.
Later, the 'Great Booster' was completed, a unit
that combines with it to enhance its flight
performance. This booster also doubled as a
powerful weapon, unleashing destructive force
comparable to a hydrogen bomb when rammed into an
enemy.
2.DSC2:
Dr. Kenzo Kabuto secretly designed and developed
this super robot based on Mazinger Z. Like Mazinger
Z, it appears from a whirlpool upon the call of
'Mazin Go!', and is completed when Tetsuya's Brain
Condor combines with its head (Fire On). Its power
source is the same Photon Power Energy as Mazinger
Z, but its armor is made of Super Alloy New Z, which
surpasses Super Alloy Z, making it even more durable
than Mazinger Z. Due to its development history,
many of its weapons were evolved and strengthened
from Mazinger Z's arsenal. Its unique attack
methods include the giant sword 'Mazinger Blade'
stored in both legs, and 'Thunder Break', which
stores lightning as energy and then unleashes it.
Additionally, a flight device called the Scramble
Dash is built into its back, allowing flight at Mach
4. Later, the 'Great Booster', which combines to
improve flight performance, was completed. It was
also a powerful weapon that, when rammed into
enemies, exhibited destructive power equivalent to a
hydrogen bomb. After the war against the Mycenae
Empire ended, it was stored in the Robot Science
Museum alongside Venus A and Boss Borot. In the
theatrical version, there was a scene where it was
seized by enemies there and fought against
Grendizer.

3.DSCR:
A female-form combat robot developed to support
Great Mazinger.
 It is completed when Jun's small jet, the
'Quinstar,' launched from a waterfall basin,
combines with its head.
 Its overall combat power falls short of Great
Mazinger's, but it carries weapons capable of
standing up to the Battle Beasts, including the
'Photon Beam' fired from both eyes, the 'Finger
Missile' launched from its fingertips, and the
rapid-fire 'Photon Missile' from its chest.
 It initially had no flight capability, but this was
later remedied by the development of the Venus
Scrander.

4.DSCR:
A giant robot built by the three doctors of the
Photon Lab after Boss pressured them into it.
 Perhaps because it was built from scrap, it seems
to be extremely fragile, and it is beaten to pieces
almost every time it fights. But it also seems easy
to repair for the same reason, and it was operated
solely by Boss and his two friends. Notably, only
its head was built to be sturdy, and it never broke
no matter what happened to it.
 After helping Mazinger Z destroy Dr. Hell's
forces, it joined Great Mazinger in standing against
the ambitions of the Mycenae Empire.
 At first it fought using nothing but the raw
strength that had let it hold its own against
Mechanical Beasts, but this proved useless against
the Battle Beasts. To compensate, Boss and his
friends developed a variety of weapons and finishing
moves through trial and error, contributing to the
fight with attacks such as the 'Drill Pressure
Punch,' built for them by the American-trained Dr.
Tobita, as well as the 'Boroboro Kick' and the
'Borot Spin Kick.'
 Boss Borot is also the only robot to appear in all
three of the original TV series. It even had a
spin-off manga serialized in a children's magazine,
leaving no doubt that it made a memorable impression
in a very different way from the lead robots.

5.DSCR:
The form Grendizer takes when combined with its
dedicated saucer-shaped mecha. The saucer-shaped
mecha alone is also called the Spazer.
 It supports Grendizer, which has no flight
capability of its own; once combined, the pair can
fly within the atmosphere at up to Mach 9 and
travel between stars via hyperspace navigation.
Like Grendizer, it runs on photon quantum energy and
is armored in space alloy Guren.
 Although some of Grendizer's own weapons become
unusable, the Spazer's various built-in armaments
were well suited to taking on large numbers of
Minifors at once.
 The enemy later discovered that combining with the
Spazer took six seconds, and began targeting that
window of vulnerability. This crisis was overcome
by combining instead with three Earth-made Spazers
developed by Dr. Umon, but as a result, the
original Spazer saw dramatically less use in battle
afterward.

6.DSCR:
A super robot developed as the guardian deity of
Planet Fleed.
 It runs on photon quantum energy, which is
dispersed throughout the cosmos, and is protected by
sturdy armor made of space alloy Guren. To prevent
misuse by others, it is equipped with a self-defense
system that unleashes an electric shock against
anyone who tries to board it without the ring that
marks the Fleed royal bloodline.
 Its main weapons include the 'Double Harken,' which
combines the crescent-shaped blades on both
shoulders, and 'Space Thunder,' which fires energy
generated from the horns on its head as an
incandescent beam; combined with its 1.8 million
horsepower, these give it extremely high combat
capability.
 It is powerful even alone, but combining with the
dedicated saucer mecha known as the Spazer
reinforces its aerial combat capability and
interstellar travel range. However, the enemy
discovered that combining with the Spazer took six
seconds, and began targeting that window of
vulnerability. This crisis was overcome by
combining instead with three Earth-made Spazers
developed by Dr. Umon, granting it even greater
mobility and combat capability.

7.DSCR:
A small saucer designed and developed by Kouji
Kabuto at NASA, and Earth's first domestically
produced UFO. Its shape closely resembles the
Adamski-type saucer, the most famous flying saucer
design at the time of the show's original
broadcast.
 It has maneuverability comparable to a Minifor and
a top flight speed of Mach 4, and it can operate at
considerable altitude within the atmosphere.
However, since it was not developed for combat, it
carries only light armament, such as small missiles
and a machine gun.
 Running on photon power, armored in Chogokin Z, and
designed by the Kabuto family, it is, in its small
way, a direct descendant of Mazinger Z. Even so,
whenever it went into battle, it was often
outmatched by Saucer Beasts and took considerable
damage. Despite its different shape, it may be
closer in role to a partner robot like Diana A.

8.DSCR:
A flying machine developed by Dr. Umon that can be
described as an Earth-made Spazer.
 Built to support Grendizer's flight capability, it
adapts Grendizer for aerial combat when combined
(Combination Cross), reaching a top speed of Mach
4.
 Its greatest advantage is that the weapons of
Grendizer, which are restricted when combined with
the original Spazer, can be used to their full
potential when combined with the Double Spazer
instead. Piloted by Kouji, it also demonstrated
high offensive performance even while separated.
 All of the Earth-made Spazers run on the same
photon quantum energy as Grendizer, but their armor
is made of Chogokin New Z.

9.DSCR:
The second Earth-made Spazer, developed by Dr.
Umon to enhance Grendizer's underwater combat
capability.
 It is a versatile machine capable of operating in
both air and water even on its own, reaching a top
underwater speed of 40 knots. However, since it
can only dive to a depth of 400 meters, Grendizer
needed to use a different mecha, the 'Ultra
Submarine,' to operate in the deep sea.
 Its greatest benefit is that, when combined with
Grendizer, it can replenish the photon quantum
energy that Grendizer consumes at a sharply
increased rate underwater. It was primarily
operated by Hikaru, and it contributed greatly to
the fight against the Vega Beasts.

10.DSCR:
The third Earth-made Spazer, built by Dr. Umon to
enable Grendizer to fight underground.
 It can operate in both air and underground even on
its own, reaching a maximum underground speed of
Mach 1. Once combined, its arm-mounted weapons
become unusable, but its 'Drill Attack,' which uses
two large drills capable of effortlessly crushing
solid bedrock, is powerful, giving it some of the
greatest offensive power among the Earth-made
Spazers.
 Kouji initially served as its pilot as well, but
once Maria appeared, control was entrusted to her.

 It tormented Grendizer with weapons such as a

14.DSCR:
Flagship of the united Vega star forces, named for

UFOs that were famous at the time.
 When the all-out attack on Earth began, Emperor
Vega personally took command and sortied aboard it.

15.DSCR:
The form completed when the Get Machines combine in
the order Dragon, Liger, and Poseidon. As with
Getter 1, the pilot remains Ryouma Nagare.
 Unlike the old Getter, which was originally built
for space development, this Getter was designed from
the start for combat. With the installation of a
Getter Ray Amplifier, it became capable of
generating over ten times the power of the old
Getter. Its armor, made of Synthetic Element Steel
G, was also made far more durable.
 It excelled in aerial combat, using the 'Getter
Beam' at range and the 'Double Tomahawk' up close,
along with the 'Mach Wing' on its back. It is the
only form that can use Getter's ultimate finishing
move, the 'Shine Spark,' and it defeated countless
powerful foes with it.

27.DSCR:
A giant robot belonging to Blue Fixer, born of the
combined scientific might of Planet S-1 and Earth.
 Blue Fixer recovered the Pulsavarn after it drifted
ashore on the Moon. They then pooled all their
available technology to modify it so it could
combine with two Earth combat machines, creating the
only machine on Earth's side capable of subspace
combat. Like the Pulsavarn, it can only be piloted
by Marin, an expert in subspace mechanics.
 Combination begins with Marin's call of "Baldios,
charge up!" It is completed when the Pulsavarn forms
the head, torso, and arms, the Baldi Prise forms the
right leg, and the Cat Ranger forms the left leg.
 It is powered by three engines - a deuterium fusion
engine, an anti-gravity engine, and a subspace
propulsion engine - and by switching between them,
it can operate anywhere. Its speed within the
atmosphere is Mach 25; in space it can fly at
30% the speed of light, and within subspace, at
infinite speed.
 Its main weapons include the 'Bal Beam,' fired from
the crystal on its forehead, the 'Pulse Saber,' a
sword stored in a chest component, and the 'Thunder
Flash,' which fires intense plasma from its chest.
27.DSC2:

 Combination begins with Marin's call of 'Baldios,

forms the left leg to complete the unit.
 It uses three engines for power: a deuterium
fusion engine, an anti-gravity engine, and a
subspace propulsion engine, and by using them
appropriately it can operate anywhere. Its speed in
the atmosphere is Mach 25. In space it can fly at
30% of lightspeed, and in subspace at infinite
speed.
 Main weapons include the beam 'Bald Beam' fired
from the crest crystal, the sword 'Pulse Saber'
stored in the chest part, and 'Thunder Flash' which
fires intense plasma from the chest.
 In Episode 26, it received reinforcement
modifications, and new armaments were added,
including 'Pulse Saber Drinking' using two Pulse
Sabers and '3D-Valdi', an attack that creates
decoys.
 Incidentally, 'Space Warrior Baldios' was broadcast
for only 31 of its 39 episodes, but since all
information about the later episodes has been
released, it is a rare anime whose full story can be
known despite the interrupted broadcast. Many
settings are hidden in the unaired portions, and
'Valdiroizer' is one of them. It was to be
Baldios's final and strongest weapon used in the
unaired Episode 38, a suicidal attack that would
destroy Baldios itself if used.

28.DSCR:
A spacecraft built to destroy the moon Ganymede,
which the Aldebaron forces had moved into position
between Earth and the Sun. In truth it was not a
spacecraft at all, but a suicide weapon with a 0%
survival rate - its pilot would have no time to
escape before being caught in Ganymede's explosion.
 Because the speed reached the speed of light when
the launch boosters were jettisoned in space,
piloting it required subspace-mechanics knowledge
and piloting skill equal to Marin's own.
 Knowing full well she would never survive, Marin
volunteered as pilot. But David, who had been
assigned to Blue Fixer as a candidate pilot for the
New Pulsavarn, also volunteered, and in the end he
was the one chosen.

37.DSCR:
A super robot developed by Dr. Kazami.
 KuRaiOh forms the upper body, KaiMeiOh the right
leg, and RikuShinOh the left leg; Big Wing then
combines over KuRaiOh to cover the chest and back,
completing the super robot God Sigma, which runs on
Trinity Energy as its power source.
 Normally the three pilots of KuRaiOh, KaiMeiOh, and
RikuShinOh remain in control as-is, but it is also
possible for the pilot of KuRaiOh alone to operate
it. In that case, however, the power of KaiMeiOh
and RikuShinOh cannot be fully utilized, which is a
drawback.
 Its armament includes the 'Finger Needle,' which
fires energy bolts from its fingertips, the 'God
Tomahawk,' which can be thrown or wielded by hand,
and the 'Spin Saucer,' a spiked disc thrown with a
sidearm motion. Its finishing move is a series of
swordsmanship techniques using the 'Musou Sword'
stored in Big Wing. Its many variations include the
'Bamboo Splitter,' 'Reverse Diagonal Cut,' 'Cross
Cut,' 'Helmet Splitter,' 'Horizontal Cut,'
'Double-Edged Thrust,' 'Double-Edged Return Cut,'
'Two-Handed Cut,' 'Lightning Cut,' and 'Straight
Cut,' among others - a truly varied repertoire.

55.DSCR:
A super robot completed when Banjo seized a
prototype Megaborg developed on Mars by Souzou Haran
and modified it.
 It has a three-stage transformation mechanism, able
to change into the heavy fighter-bomber Daifighter
and the heavy tank Daitank. It houses the small
variable fighter Mach Attacker inside, and that
unit's cockpit block moves through the machine's
body to become Daitarn 3's pilot seat.
 Its main weapons include the beam-bladed sword
'Daitarn Zanbar,' the fan-shaped 'Daitarn Fan,'
which can also be used as a shield, and the 'Daitarn
Web,' whose arm-mounted cross transforms into a
shuriken. Beyond these, it carries numerous other
weapons built into its whole body, including
missiles, cannons, and snappers.
 Its ultimate finishing move, the 'Sun Attack,'
fires a bolt of light from the sun disc on its
forehead with the call, "Lend me the power of the
sun - now, my finishing blow, Sun Attack!" Other
variations of this call also exist, and on occasion
the call was made without the attack actually being
fired.

58.DSCR:
The machine completed when Kei's beloved mount, the
Bronco II, was severely damaged and, during repairs,
was reinforced and modified using Emaan technology.
 The Bronco II's legs were kept as they were, while
its arms were replaced at Kei's request, since he
had liked the handling of the M.Lover's arms when
he piloted it. Furthermore, by adding a psycho
system along with three inertial control systems,
two anti-gravity levitation devices, and a nuclear
reactor with output approaching 500,000
horsepower, it came to surpass the performance of
the old Drifand despite being a hastily assembled
machine. Thanks to its high performance, a
mass-production model was later developed as well.
 Beyond its robot form, the Orgaroid, another major
feature is its shape-shifting capability (VARIABLE
GEOMETRY), which lets it take four forms as the
situation demands: Flyer, GERWALK, and Tank.
 When it was completed, there was a scene in which
the members of the Factory discussed what to call
the new Bronco II, with everyone freely proposing
names like 'Valhalla' and 'Gammon.' In the end, it
was named 'Orguss,' after the name of a god of war
from the world Jabby came from. Incidentally,
'Nebulard,' one of the proposed names, was the
show's working title during its planning stage.

60.DSCR:
One of the mass-production Orguss units developed
in the Emaan homeland after its performance was
recognized. This is the machine piloted by Olson,
who had taken refuge with the Factory. It differs
from both the standard mass-production units and
Kei's Orguss in its color scheme and the shape of
its head and legs.
 To ease its handling difficulty, the
mass-production units' engines were fitted with a
limiter, but on Olson's unit, that limiter was
removed in consideration of his piloting skill. As
a result, it is the highest-performing machine among
all those bearing the Orguss name.

62.DSCR:
A Drifand piloted by Maaie.
 The Moraba was developed in the 17th year of the
Chaotic Era for purposes such as escorting
factories, and stands as a pioneering example of
Emaan devices.
 Its simple structure makes it easy to modify,
resulting in numerous derivative variants depending
on the factory operating it or the pilot flying it.
Its shoulders and arms can also be folded in to
reduce air resistance.
 Maaie's unit is a relatively standard, lightly
armed type equipped with a five-barrel Gatling
Cannon and a Grenade Gun, and it excels in
maneuverability and mobility.

63.DSCR:
A Drifand piloted by Lieea. Kei also rode in it
once.
 Where Maaie's unit is close to the standard type,
Lieea's has been extensively modified in terms of
armament. Though ill-suited to high-mobility
combat, it boasts increased firepower thanks to
equipment such as a large Missile Gun pod, a grenade
launcher, and a missile guidance system, and it
excels at hit-and-run tactics.
 The Moraba is also equipped with the sympathetic
response system later adapted for use in the Orguss
as well. By transmitting the pilot's thoughts
directly to the machine, it allows reflexive
movement even in situations where mechanical
piloting alone could not react in time. Thanks to
this system, even an inexperienced pilot can manage
a certain degree of combat.

64.DSCR:
A second-generation Gerwalk (biped) weapon used by

and Olson belonged.
 Besides high-speed combat in Flyer Form, it can
also fight on the ground in Gerwalk Form. Its legs
serve not only as landing gear but also house
thrusters at their base that boost propulsion during
flight.
 Though it has no arms, a manipulator is built into

this manipulator to activate an unadjusted
space-time oscillation bomb, an accident that sent
him and the Bronco II flying twenty years into the

65.DSCR:
A commercial vessel built for Emaan people to
conduct trade wherever they travel. The factory led
by Shaya also makes use of this ship.
 Its exterior, with a red roof and white walls,
looks exactly like a house out of a storybook. The
resemblance goes beyond appearance too - wooden
furnishings and landscape paintings decorate its
interior, and it is even equipped with sports
facilities and a public-bath-style bathing area,
giving it a strong sense of being a living space for
the factory's crew. Even so, it also houses mecha
hangars and workshops capable of repair and
assembly.
 The Chiram call it by the code name 'House.'

66.DSCR:

number RSG-21A-1.
 Though it uses the same legs as the Ishkick, its
cockpit is a vertically stacked two-seater, with an
operator on top and a pilot below, securing a wide
field of view.
 To avoid detection by enemy craft, its propulsion
system is built with excellent sound and infrared
suppression. It also mounts a compact reactor with
a quiet drive despite its low output, among various
other features tailored to its role as a
reconnaissance craft.

67.DSCR:
A third-generation combat device developed by the
Chiram military to establish a new weapons system
suited to the chaos-torn world. Model number
MBG-21D-2.
 It is a legged fighter of the type commonly called
Gerwalk in Chiram weaponry, and it appears to be
produced in enormous numbers as a mainline unit. It
incorporates the new anti-gravity system technology,
which, while limiting its top speed, greatly
improves its mobility.
 Its firepower is formidable, combining a
large-caliber Beam Cannon on the front of the
fuselage with sixteen loaded Missiles. The
ultra-thick steel plating used on the front of its
legs serves double duty, both for inertial
maneuvering and as a blunt weapon in close combat.

68.DSCR:
A commander-type Ishkick modified for use by unit
commanders. Model number MBG-21F-1.
 It adds an abundance of weaponry, including a
90mm rapid-fire grenade cannon, a large-caliber
Beam Cannon with adjustable output, and 20mm twin
AutoGuns, along with an advanced detection system.
 Its full loaded weight approaches the 30-ton
carrying limit, and although auxiliary Boosters have
been fitted to ease the load on its legs, its
operational time is still considerably shortened.
It is also difficult to pilot, causing problems that
can hinder mission operations, among other issues.
Even so, it remains popular among confident
commanders and continues to see frontline use.

72.DSCR:
A fourth-generation combat device developed by the
Chiram military to counter the Mu. This is the
standard type piloted by regular soldiers, model
number MBG-24A.
 To handle a variety of combat situations
single-handedly, it has a variable-form function
allowing it to take three forms: Battle Form, Flyer
Form, and Gerwalk Form.
 Compared to the Ishkick, it has twice the mass and
six times the output, making it quite a heavyweight
machine by Chiram standards, with performance nearly
on par with the Orguss. It is likewise capable of
inertial control, but since much of its inertial
control system remains underdeveloped, it is less
reliable than the Orguss in this regard.

75.DSCR:
A Drifand used by Emaan. It can be equipped with
the same type of Missile Gun and missile pack used
on the Orguss, and it saw extensive use in Manisha's
unit as well.
 Emaan devices are fitted with an Inertial Control
System capable of negating the mass of matter. This
eliminates the effects of gravity, allowing for easy
rapid acceleration, sudden stops, and sharp turns,
while also reducing the G-forces exerted on the
pilot to almost nothing. Thanks to this benefit,
the machine can operate under nearly any conditions,
so long as air resistance is taken into account.
 As various manipulators were developed to improve
work efficiency and combat capability, this
eventually led to the arms it carries today. This
is why it is called a Drifand, short for 'Drift
Hand.'

 Its outstanding mobility and output, along with its
wide array of optional weaponry, all far surpass
those of conventional Walker Machines.
 Its drawback is poor maintainability stemming from
the complexity of its mechanisms. Even Cattset's
skill reportedly struggled with it - there were
malfunctions where, after transforming, the head
would get stuck and fail to emerge.
 Two units existed. One had its wings destroyed by

thereafter operated as the Sub Xabungle. It was
later destroyed in battle against the Greta Gully.

77.DSCR:
The most advanced large Walker Machine created by
the Innocent. After losing the Xabungle, Jiron
seized this unit and operated it aboard the Iron
Gear from then on.
 While matching the Xabungle in mobility, it is
improved across the board in maneuverability, armor,
and firepower. The combination mechanism that was
the Xabungle's greatest weak point has been greatly
simplified in this unit, resulting in an all-around
machine with excellent maintainability as well.
 Its firepower is high, thanks to dedicated weapons
such as the Boomerang Idiom and a five-tube rocket
launcher, along with a Bazooka wrested away from the
female warrior Tron. It also possesses powerful
hover capability, allowing for standalone flight,
though not with complete freedom of movement.

78.DSCR:
The first of three landships built to the Iron Gear
type. Its greatest feature is its ability to
transform into Walker Machine form.
 Provided by the Innocent to Elche's father, Kyarin,
it possesses overwhelming combat power. On the
other hand, it is something of a prototype vessel,
with lingering issues in fuel efficiency and
maintainability, frequently breaking down and
infuriating Cattset, who handles its piloting and
upkeep.
 The original Iron Gear was badly damaged in battle
against its sister ship, the second Iron Gear-type
vessel, the Greta Gully. Even so, it won that
battle, and by capturing the Greta Gully and
repainting it, it has been put into service as the
second-generation Iron Gear.

79.DSCR:
The state of the Iron Gear transformed into Walker
Machine form.
 The transformation mechanism from landship to
Walker Machine is fitted only to the Iron Gear type,
and its combat strength is unmatched by anything
else. That said, this comes at a considerable cost
to the airframe. There are also numerous points
that could stand improvement, such as a major drop
in mobility and a lack of means to attack targets to
its rear.
 Surprisingly, it is also dexterous, having even
been seen untying, on its own, the knot of the
head-wrap it wore as snowfield camouflage.
 Despite its massive size, it is capable of soaring
high into the air and diving down to attack. Its
offensive power is unrivaled, but if cargo aboard is
not secured, considerable damage inside the ship can
be expected.

103.DSCR:
A mobile suit independently developed by the Titans
aboard Gryps I.
 It is a redesign of the original Gundam, but by
abolishing the Core Block System and adopting a
Movable Frame, it achieves high maneuverability.
New technologies are also incorporated throughout
the airframe, including a linear-seat cockpit with a
full panoramic monitor and a detachable Vulcan pod
system.
 After it was seized from the Titans by Kamille and
his allies, its color scheme was changed from black
to white.
 By combining with the later-developed G-Defenser,
it became possible to boost firepower and armor and
extend its cruising range.
103.DSC2:
The Titans developed this mobile suit independently
at Gryps I. It is a redesign of the original
Gundam, but it abolishes the core block system and
achieves high mobility through the adoption of a
movable frame. New technologies are also
incorporated throughout the machine, including a
linear-seat cockpit with a panoramic monitor and a
detachable vulcan pod system. After being seized
from the Titans by Kamille and others, its color
scheme was changed from black to white. By
combining with the G-Defenser, which was developed
later, it became possible to improve firepower,
armor, and extend its cruising range.
 It was developed by Anaheim Electronics, and became
the AEUG's transformable mobile suit. It is the
culmination of the know-how cultivated in the Z
Project, combining the movable frame technology of
the Gundam Mk-II with the idea of the Flying Armor.
The adoption of Gundarium Gamma armor and a new
generator achieved outstanding mobility. In
addition, it became possible to use the Hyper Mega
Launcher, a handheld weapon with power comparable to
the Mega Bazooka Launcher. Furthermore, by
transforming into the Waverider, it demonstrates
tremendous range and acceleration. It is a machine
capable of performing in all situations, such as
atmospheric entry on its own, independent flight
within the atmosphere, and combat operations
carrying a wingman on its back. Later, the
installation of the Bio-Sensor, a simplified
psycommu, gave it the ability to follow Kamille's
sharpened reactions. At the same time, however,
inexplicable phenomena not included in the
specifications were also confirmed, such as
interfering with enemy mobile suit movements and
stopping them.

104.DSCR:
The state of the G-Defenser combined with the
Gundam Mk-II's backpack area. Also called the Mk-II
Defenser, it can also transform into its cruising
form, the G-Flyer.
 Amid the astonishing pace at which mobile suit
development was advancing, the performance gap of
the Gundam Mk-II had already become pronounced, and
these Parts were manufactured to power it up. With
increased firepower, reinforced side and rear armor,
and an enlarged backpack section that extends
cruising range, its performance reaches a level that
approaches even the Zeta Gundam. In particular, the
G-Defenser's greatest weapon, the Long Beam Rifle,
holds extraordinary destructive power even among
firearms a mobile suit can carry.

Waverider, it demonstrates immense range and
acceleration. It is a unit capable of operating in
all situations, including atmospheric entry on its
own, solo flight within the atmosphere, and carrying
a wingman on its back for combat operations. Later,
with the installation of the Bio-Sensor, a
simplified psycommu, it gained responsiveness that
tracked Kamille's honed reactions. However, at the
same time, the manifestation of inexplicable
phenomena not included in the specifications was
also confirmed, such as interfering with the
movements of enemy mobile suits to halt them.

107.DSCR:
The cruising form of the Zeta Gundam.
 It can be used as an aerial and space fighter, or
to carry an allied unit on its back, but its
greatest feature is that it makes standalone
atmospheric reentry possible.
 It is called the Waverider because it derives lift
from the compressed shock wave formed along the
underside of its hull.

108.DSCR:
A prototype mobile suit born from the AEUG's Zeta
Project, developed by Anaheim Electronics.
 It was originally one of the design candidates for
the Zeta Gundam, but development was halted due to
flaws in its variable mechanism, and it was later
redesigned as a non-transforming unit. Its
performance is high, and thanks in particular to its
adoption of a Movable Frame and Wing Binders, it
became a machine boasting maneuverability among the
very best.
 It has numerous conspicuous visual features,
including its vivid gold body color and the
character for 'hundred' emblazoned on both
shoulders.

Electronics for the AEUG.

121.DSCR:
A variable mobile armor developed by the Earth
Federation Forces.
 It is the first machine to enable a mobile suit to
fly independently within an atmosphere.
 In mobile armor form, its shape gives it excellent
durability and resistance to enemy fire, along with
outstanding aerial combat capability. Its
performance in mobile suit form was also excellent,
leading to widespread deployment at Federation bases
in the TV version. In the theatrical version,
however, only the one unit piloted by Bran Bltark
appears.

122.DSCR:
A variable mobile armor originally developed for
space use but repurposed for high-altitude
interception.
 Both arms are fitted with active thruster units
that can freely redirect their thrust, giving it
explosive acceleration especially in mobile armor
form. However, this comes at the cost of extreme
G-forces, making it a machine that only a few pilots
- such as the enhanced human Rosamia or the high
G-tolerance Yazan - could handle.
 It is capable of operating within an atmosphere,
but its propellant consumption is severe, making
long flights impossible without additional
boosters. Early production units also suffered from
a blind spot in the lower portion of the panoramic
screen due to insufficient adjustment.

123.DSCR:
The first mobile armor developed by Paptimus
Scirocco aboard the Jupitris.
 Built to withstand the gravity of the Jupiter
sphere, roughly 40% of the airframe is taken up by
boosters and thruster units. With this mass
concentrated at the rear in mobile armor form, it
displays especially high mobility.
 It carries powerful built-in armaments, including
mega particle cannons integrated with its back
thrusters and arm-mounted grenade launchers. It can
also transform into mobile suit form for close
combat, making it a well-balanced, excellent
machine.

124.DSCR:
A variable mobile suit of the Titans, developed
under Scirocco's leadership.
 Besides mobile suit and mobile armor forms, it can
also fight in an intermediate, half-man half-horse
form.
 It is armed with the powerful Fedayeen Rifle,
comparable to a warship's main gun, for long range,
and the Movable Frame Claw for close combat,
allowing it to fight effectively at any distance.
 The fact that it drove Kamille's Gundam Mk-II to
the brink of destruction speaks to its high
performance.

for flexible responses in combat, and it is also
easy to mass-produce.
 Its unique special weapon, the Shock Wire (also
called the Snake), delivers powerful electric
attacks that damage not only the machine but the
pilot as well. The squadron led by Yazan
demonstrated high combat effectiveness by
coordinating three units together.

psycommu system was later removed so that any pilot

the Jupitris.
 A firepower-focused machine, it is intended to

129.DSCR:
A giant variable mobile armor developed at the
Murasame Research Institute, a Newtype research
facility, and the Earth Federation Forces' first
Newtype-exclusive machine.
 Its pilot is Four Murasame, who came from the
Murasame Research Institute. The psycommu system,
conventionally used only for machine control and
weapons management, is also used by her for remote
guidance of the unit. Perhaps because of this
power, it places an enormous strain on the pilot's
mind, producing a side effect that seems to bind the
pilot to the machine as if under a curse.
 It carries triple mega particle cannons, beam
cannons, and other weapons throughout its frame, and
the sight of it wrapping Hong Kong City in flames
with its excessive firepower is nothing short of a
black devil made manifest. It is also capable of
flight using a Minovsky Craft system, though only in
mobile armor form.

numerous vernier thrusters throughout its body give
it mobility greater than its appearance suggests.
Its armaments are distinctive as well, including a
beam tomahawk and a shield that can also function as
a beam gun.

131.DSCR:
A Newtype-exclusive mobile suit developed by Axis.
 It was designed on the concept of a mobile suit
version of the Elmeth, the mobile armor of the
former Principality of Zeon.
 The Elmeth's greatest feature was its remote attack
terminals, the Bits, but their built-in generators
made a certain amount of bulk unavoidable. However,
the Funnels equipped on the Qubeley use an energy
CAP system, achieving considerable downsizing.
Psycommu control extends beyond the Funnels to
direct control of the machine itself.

132.DSCR:
A large mobile suit developed by Scirocco aboard
the Jupitris.
 Its frame is equipped with reaction attitude
control systems and rocket motors throughout, and a
Bio-Sensor built into the cockpit gives it excellent
responsiveness. Despite the sluggish impression its
appearance gives, it possesses top-class mobility
and maneuverability.
 Its armaments are equally formidable, including a
large beam rifle uniquely modified by Scirocco
himself, and hip-mounted sub-manipulators (Arms)
that wield beam sabers. It can rightly be called
one of the strongest mobile suits of the Gryps
Conflict.

133.DSCR:
An assault space cruiser serving as the AEUG's
flagship.
 Modeled after the White Base, which distinguished
itself during the One Year War, it was secretly
developed by Brigadier General Blex at the colony
'Sweetwater'. It was initially called the White
Base II, but was ultimately named the Argama at the
whim of its financial backers.
 Its armor is more robust than it appears, and it
carries a total of three main cannons at the ship's
center and underside, plus two deflection-type mega
particle cannons on its lower flanks. Combined with
the high command ability of its captain, Bright Noa,
it achieved numerous victories.
 It is equipped with a residential block that
generates simulated gravity through centrifugal
force by rotating, a sight that can be seen during
the opening.

134.DSCR:
A newly built AEUG warship constructed at Amman on
the Moon.
 It is equipped with three mobile suit catapults at
the bow and one at the stern, and carries a large
number of mobile suits.
 Henken, the first captain of the Argama, commands
this ship, and it has performed on par with the
Argama under Bright's command.
 It is said to be one of four Irish-type ships built
at Amman, though no other sister ships appear in the
theatrical version.
134.DSC2:
This is a new AEUG battleship built at Amman on the
Moon. It is equipped with three mobile suit
catapults at the front and one at the rear, and has
a large mobile suit carrying capacity. Henken, the
former captain of the first Argama, served as its
captain, and it performed comparably to the Argama
under Bright's command. It is said to be one of
four Irish-class ships built at Amman, but no other
ships of the same class appear in the theatrical
version. In the final battle, it advanced to shield
Emma, who was being toyed with by a Hambrabi, and
was shot down and sunk by Yazan. The fact that this
action, which was Henken's unilateral decision in
the TV version, was changed to the consensus of the
bridge in the theatrical version shows how popular
Emma was with the crew in the latter.

135.DSCR:

the Earth Federation Forces' mainstay during the One

141.DSCR:
A prototype mobile suit developed by Anaheim
Electronics for the purpose of mass-producing the
Zeta Gundam. Its name is an abbreviation of
"Refined Gundam Zeta."
 Its transformation mechanism has been eliminated;
instead, it reaches cruising form by combining with
a Back Weapon System that envelops the airframe.
However, because the system is jettisoned when
transforming into mobile suit form, it cannot be
re-equipped on the spot once separated, leaving the
machine lacking in flexibility.
 It combines high mobility and firepower, and its
performance as a mobile suit is extremely high in
its own right. However, its production cost proved
too high, and mass production was abandoned. The
single completed unit was assigned to Londo Bell,
which was pursuing Neo Zeon.
141.DSC2:
A prototype mobile suit developed by Anaheim
Electronics with the aim of mass-producing the Zeta
Gundam. Its name is an abbreviation for 'Refined
Gundam Zeta.' The transformation mechanism was
eliminated, and it achieves a cruising form by
combining with the Back Weapon System that envelops
the machine. However, since the system is
jettisoned when transforming to mobile suit form,

However, due to its high production cost, mass

assigned to the Londo Bell unit pursuing Neo Zeon.
Amuro used it in the early stages, and Kayra took
over in the middle stages. In the final stages,
Chan boarded it to deliver the Psycho Frame to
Amuro. However, it was shot down by a beam fired by
Hathaway, who had flown into a rage at Quess's
death.

142.DSCR:
A Newtype-exclusive mobile suit developed by
Anaheim Electronics at the request of Londo Bell.
Its pilot, Amuro Ray, handled its design himself.
 Developed by analyzing the performance of Gundams
throughout history and incorporating the latest
technology, it was completed as an
ultra-high-performance machine that belies its
rushed production.
 A Psycho Frame built into the area around the
cockpit gives it extraordinary mobility and
responsiveness. It is also the first Gundam-type
mobile suit capable of using the Fin Funnel, a
psycommu weapon. These are larger than ordinary
funnels, and correspondingly more powerful. Beyond
attack use, several units can be linked together to
generate an I Field, forming an anti-beam barrier,
making them useful for both offense and defense.
 To prevent Neo Zeon's attempt to drop Axis onto
Earth, it fought and won a decisive battle against
Char's Sazabi, which was likewise equipped with a
Psycho Frame.
142.DSC2:
Anaheim Electronics developed this Newtype-only
mobile suit in response to a request from the Londe
Bell. The pilot, Amuro, was personally in charge of
its design. Because it was developed by analyzing
the performance of past Gundams and incorporating
the latest technology, it was completed as an
ultra-high-performance machine that seemed anything
but hastily built. The Psycho Frame built into the
cockpit area achieves exceptional mobility and
response. It is also the first Gundam-type mobile
suit to use the psycommu weapon Fin Funnel. These
are larger than normal funnels and correspondingly
more powerful. Besides use as a weapon, several
units can be linked together to generate an I Field
and form an anti-beam barrier, making it useful for
both offense and defense. In order to stop Neo
Zeon's Axis drop, he challenged Char's Sazabi, which
also had a Psycho Frame, to a decisive battle and
won. Afterwards, he struggled to push Axis back.
His figure inspired other machines, regardless of
ally or enemy, to follow, and the hearts of all who
witnessed it became one. At that time, a shining
force field was formed by the Psycho Frame, and its
influence altered the trajectory of Axis.

143.DSCR:
A mobile suit that emerged from the White Doll, an
object enshrined at the foot of Mountain Cycle in
the Ingressa territory of Vicinity.
 At first it had almost no armaments, fighting in
melee with its bare hands or a beam saber. Later, a
rifle, shield, hammer, and other equipment were
excavated, and equipping these steadily improved its
combat power.
 It operates via the I Field Beam Drive (IFBD),
which spreads an internally generated I Field across
the airframe's surface and controls the machine by
manipulating it. Since it carries no generator, its
internal structure has ample room to spare, and the
Multi-Purpose Silo (a general-purpose weapons cache)
installed in its chest can be loaded with a variety
of armaments as needed. Loran in fact used it to
carry all manner of things, from nuclear missiles to
cattle.
 Its nanomachine-coated armor has self-repair
capability, and given enough time it can even
regenerate missing parts.
 The Moonlight Butterfly (M-Fly) system, arguably
Turn A Gundam's greatest feature, scatters
nanomachines carried on an I Field, and is said to
have destroyed the scientific civilization of the
previous century.
 The cockpit in the waist can separate and transform
into the Core Fighter. It has almost no combat
power of its own, but it is an indispensable part
for properly using the Moonlight Butterfly system.
 Only a few characters in the story call it "Gundam"
- Loran and most others instead call it the 'White
Doll' or the 'White Beard.'

 Attaching skirt-shaped aerial maneuvering units to

150.DSCR:
A large anti-ship combat mobile suit of the Dianna
Counter.
 Its name is short for Walking Dome, and true to
that name, the dome on its head houses an array of
weapons, including anti-air Vulcan cannons and an
anti-ship beam cannon. Its bombardment is powerful
enough to reshape mountains.
 Armor coated in nano-skin gives it self-repair
capability, and it excels in both firepower and
armor. However, its huge frame and heavy armament
leave it weak in close combat, as shown when Turn A
Gundam severed its wrist with a hand chop.
 Within the Militia it was nicknamed the
'Scarecrow.'

152.DSCR:
A melee-focused mobile suit excavated from Mountain
Cycle on the Moon and independently modified by
Corin. Its main armament is the Minchi Drill,
likewise modified by Corin from civilian excavation

 Making use of a spine structure running from head
to tail, it can transform into a high-speed walking
form reminiscent of a dinosaur. In this form, it
can deliver headbutts using its head like a blunt
weapon.

153.DSCR:
The main mobile suit of the Ghingnham fleet.
 In addition to the overwhelming firepower of the
mega particle cannon built into its toroidal
shield-mounted right shoulder, it possesses
excellent aerial combat ability and mobility,
surpassing the SUMO in overall performance.
 It is the only machine with an artificial
muscle-fiber drive system, and it is speculated that
it was originally equipped with a 'Mobile Trace
System' that captured the pilot's myoelectric
signals and fed them back into the machine's
movements.

154.DSCR:
A mobile suit excavated from Mountain Cycle on the
Moon.
 Several units were excavated, but aside from the
one piloted by Merribeth, the rest are unmanned
drones that move in coordination with it.
 It possesses unique armaments, including Oozy Armor
(secretion armor) that hardens nanomachines to
improve bullet resistance, and a group of Squeeze
Weapons designed to destroy enemy machines without
killing their pilots. Because of this, it truly
shows its worth in anti-mobile-suit combat.
 It is also unusual in having a cockpit designed to
be operated while standing.

155.DSCR:
A mobile suit excavated from Mountain Cycle on the
Moon.
 Called a Turn-type machine like Turn A Gundam, the
two cause a resonance phenomenon when they sense
each other's presence.
 Unlike Turn A Gundam, its cockpit is located in the
head, allowing it to function independently. It can
also separate its entire body into nine parts to
perform all-range attacks, and can restrain enemies
to steal their data. Through this ability it
absorbed Turn A Gundam's data, gaining the ability
to use the Moonlight Butterfly (M-Fly) as well.
 It has a nanomachine-based self-repair function,
but an X-shaped scar on its chest, said to have been
inflicted by Turn A Gundam in the past, remains to
this day for reasons unknown.
 The origin of the name 'X' is said to mean 'that
which had its path bent by the tenth (X) star.'

However, it possesses more defensive power than its
looks suggest, including a powerful I Field.
 The bow section can also separate to operate as a
mobile command post.

 It is equipped with a giant beam saber generated at

158.DSCR:
A mobile suit developed by the former Federation
Forces during the Seventh Space War.
 With its Flash System, capable of controlling bit
mobile suits, and its Satellite Cannon, powerful
enough to destroy a colony, it becomes the strongest
weapon of all in the hands of a Newtype pilot.
 The unit piloted by Garrod is one of several
produced. Unlike the Gundam Airmaster and Gundam
Leopard developed around the same time, it requires
a G Controller - doubling as both the right control
lever and the Satellite Cannon's firing trigger - to
be attached before it can be activated.

159.DSCR:
A machine reinforced and modified by Kid, using
"some amazing parts he'd kept in reserve," to
compensate for the firepower shortfall of the Gundam
X after its Satellite Cannon was destroyed in the
battle with the Vertigo.
 Though it has lost the Satellite Cannon, equipping
the Divider for which it is named allows it to
maintain stable performance even without the moon in
the sky.
 The Divider, also known as the Harmonica Cannon,
combines the functions of a multi-barrel beam
cannon, a deployable shield, and propulsion
verniers. It is a versatile weapon that provides a
range of benefits, from offense and defense to
improved mobility.

160.DSCR:
A machine reinforced and modified from the Gundam
Airmaster after it was heavily damaged in battle
with the New Federation Forces. It is the
crystallization of facilities and materials provided
by General Lee of the Republic of Estard, combined
with the ideas and skill of Kid, who was "moved" by
seeing them.
 At a glance, the change in the machine's color from
red to blue draws the most attention, but this refit
actually focuses on improving the firepower that was
the Airmaster's greatest weakness. In particular,
replacing the nose Vulcan with a beam cannon allows
it to display high combat power in flight mode.
 Large boosters at the wingtips also improved its
thrust, to the point that it can now carry the
Gundam Leopard riding on top while flying, whereas
before it had to carry it by lifting it.
 By design, combining with the G Falcon could
theoretically produce output exceeding that of a
cruiser-class warship, but this was never put to use
in actual combat.

cruiser-class warship, but this was never put to
use in actual combat.

161.DSCR:
A machine that was actually reinforced and modified
after Kid, upon seeing the Gundam Leopard heavily
damaged in battle with the New Federation Forces,
declared, "A full overhaul would be faster than
fixing it."
 The machine's color was changed from green to a
red-based scheme, further boosting its already high
firepower.
 Many of its originally solid-round-heavy weapons
were replaced with beam weapons. In particular, the
inner-arm gatling gun on its right arm was replaced
with twin beam cylinders mounted on both arms,
converting it from a solid-round weapon to a beam
weapon and doubling the number of barrels, resulting
in more than twice its effective firepower.
 Combining with the G Falcon finally made possible
the aerial operation Roybea had long wished for.
However, the battlefield shifted to space
immediately afterward, so it was never put to use in
actual combat.

162.DSCR:
Based on the Gundam X, this mobile suit was
developed by the Government Reconstruction Committee
with the aim of creating 'a new Gundam possessing
tremendous power as a symbol.'
 Its base was the unit Jamil piloted during the
Seventh Space War, but so much cutting-edge
technology has been incorporated internally that it
can fairly be called an entirely new model. Katock,
however, calls it "a fifteen-year-old ghost."
 The Satellite Cannon, the Gundam X's greatest
feature, has been doubled into the Twin Satellite
Cannon. Its output has more than doubled as well,
making it powerful enough to destroy even the
artificial island Zonder Epta or a Colony Laser.
 Not only the Satellite Cannon but the unit's
output, mobility, and maneuverability have all seen
dramatic improvements across the board. In its
first battle, despite fighting alone and without
even a rifle, it shot down as many as eight
Varients, a testament to its outstanding
performance.
 However, the dedicated Buster Rifle is no longer
integrated with the shield, and this has proven a
drawback in terms of durability, leading to it being
destroyed on several occasions. Because of this,
the pilot was once forced to borrow a rifle from the
Gundam Airmaster to keep fighting.

163.DSCR:
The combined form of the Gundam Double X and the
G-Falcon.
 The G-Falcon's B-Parts, moved to the back, function
as an energy pack, allowing the Twin Satellite
Cannon to fire at maximum output as well as enabling
rapid-fire shots.
 There is also a cruising form in which the Gundam
Double X is sandwiched between the G-Falcon's A- and
B-Parts; the overall length and weight listed here
are those of that configuration.

164.DSCR:
A high-mobility support fighter developed by the
old Federation Forces to support Gundam-type mobile
suits.
 It was a prototype that never saw actual combat;
left drifting in space in a half-destroyed state, it
was recovered and restored for use by Pala and the
rest of the anti-Space Revolutionary Army
organization Satelicon.
 It consists of a cockpit section (A-Parts) and a
booster section (B-Parts), and by housing (combining
with) a Gundam-type mobile suit between the two
parts, it can enhance that unit's strengths or
compensate for its weaknesses. In practice,
however, it combined with the Gundam Double X only a
handful of times, combined with the Gundam Leopard
Destroy just once as a test, and never combined with
the Gundam Airmaster Burst at all.
 Even alone it boasts excellent mobility and
firepower, and it distinguished itself by shooting
down numerous Septems and Daughtress Neos.
 Along with the Gundam Double X, it is one of the
few units to be named in a subtitle.

165.DSCR:
An Alps-class land battleship captained by Jamil.
 Though officially classified as a 'land
battleship,' it can also travel across water via
hovering, giving it a wide operational range.
 It can carry up to six mobile suits, with the
Gundam X, Gundam Airmaster, and Gundam Leopard
serving as its primary complement.
 It also serves as a living space for its pilots,
including Garrod and the others. When Roabey became
a permanent employee aboard the Freeden, she had a
relaxation room installed at her own expense to make
the voyage more comfortable.

166.DSCR:
A mobile suit used as a mainstay by the Space
Revolutionary Army during the Seventh Space War.
The unit Ennil uses is an improved model, purchased
from Lumark of the Sea Vultures and repainted in her
personal color, blue.
 It has been considerably reinforced in propulsion
and other areas compared to a standard Jenice, and
thanks in part to Ennil's own skill, it was able to
hold its own even against the new-model Varients.
 For the final battle it was refitted for space
combat and launched into space together with the
Freeden II.
166.DSC2:
A mobile suit that the Space Revolutionary Army

the Sea Vulture trader Rumark and painted in her
personal color, blue. Its propulsion and other

with the speed of the high-performance machines such

the Freeden II. That was a modest yet important
role: protecting the place for everyone to return
to.

167.DSCR:
A mobile armor built by Lumark of the Sea Vultures,
with whom Ennil was on close terms, out of salvaged
parts.
 Its mobility leaves nothing to be desired - when
Ennil happened to witness the Gundam Double X and
was subsequently pursued by the New Federation
Forces, it managed to outrun even the new-model
Varient mobile suits. However, due to insufficient
firepower it was unable to stand up to a Gundam; it
was caught by the Gundam Ashtaron and shot down by
the Gundam Vassago.
 The unit's name means 'hope' in Lumark's native
tongue.
167.DSC2:
A mobile armor that Rumark, a Sea Vulture trader
with whom Ennil was close, built from salvaged
parts. Its mobility was impeccable - when Ennil
happened to witness the Gundam Double X and was
pursued by the New Federation Forces, she outran the
new-model mobile suit Varient. However, due to
insufficient firepower, it could not match the
Gundams; it was captured by the Gundam Ashtaron and
shot down by the Gundam Virsago. The unit's name
means 'hope' in the language of Rumark's homeland.
For Ennil, who began traveling with the Freeden
after it was shot down by the Frost Brothers, this
was truly the machine that brought her hope.

168.DSCR:
A mobile suit created by upgrading the Gundam
Vassago for space combat.
 Modifications extend down to the smallest details,
including reinforcement of the Strike Claw's attack
power and shock-absorption capacity, and removal of
the inner frame's armor.
 The Mega Sonic Cannon, its greatest feature, has
gained an additional two barrels on the chest to
become the Triple Mega Sonic Cannon, further
sharpening its already fearsome destructive power to
match its menacing appearance. The chest armor,
shaped to resemble a face, opens when the Triple
Mega Sonic Cannon is fired, embodying the unit's
name, Chest Break.
 The Satellite Launcher, used together with the
Gundam Ashtaron HC, requires successful control of
the Satellite System, but its power rivals that of
the Twin Satellite Cannon.

169.DSCR:
A unit created by upgrading the Gundam Ashtaron for
space combat.
 Its greatest feature, the 'Trans-System' mechanism
for morphing into mobile armor form, remains
intact. Not only its defensive strength but also
its mobility in mobile armor form is high enough to
rival the G-Falcon both within and outside the
atmosphere. When morphing, roughly half the unit's
body is stored within its greatly enlarged backpack,
giving it a shape that embodies its name, Hermit
Crab.
 In addition to the enlarged Atomic Scissors and the
change from the Scissors Beam Cannon to the Scissors
Cannon, it is also equipped with the Satellite
Launcher, though the conditions for its use are
demanding - it requires successful control of the
Satellite System and can only be used together with
the Gundam Vassago CB. This gives it attack power
that rivals even the Gundam Double X.

170.DSCR:
A prototype mobile suit developed by the New
Federation Forces.
 Like the Gundam-type units, it is equipped with the
Flash System, allowing a Newtype pilot to remotely
control five Bit Mobile Suits. Unlike the Bit
Mobile Suits used by Gundam-type units, the
Rashvent's Bit Mobile Suits are identical in
appearance to the main unit itself, making it
difficult for enemies to single it out in battle.
 Piloted by Abel, whose Newtype abilities blossomed
over the course of the fighting, it held its own -
and more - against Garrod, Jamil, and Witz all at
once.
170.DSC2:

Garrod, Jamil, and Witz simultaneously. However,
the battle was decided when Garrod, acting on
Tiffa's advice, saw through the decoy and landed a
decisive blow on the real unit.

171.DSCR:
A high-mobility mobile armor developed by the New
Federation Forces.
 With a fighter-jet-like form, a cockpit resembling
a mobile suit's head, and a beam rifle gripped at
the barrel by a manipulator, its shape stands out
considerably compared to other mobile suits and
mobile armors.
 Designed with the goal of securing air superiority,
it moderately damaged the Gundam Airmaster in an
aerial battle against it.
171.DSC2:

other mobile suits and mobile armors. It was
designed to secure air supremacy, and in an aerial
battle against the Gundam Airmaster, it heavily
damaged its opponent. However, it was shot down in
an instant by the improved Gundam Airmaster Burst.

172.DSCR:
A mobile suit developed by the New Federation
Forces as an evolution of the Daughtress.
 The Wired Beam Rifles mounted on both arms can be
used as beam cutters at close range or as
beam-firing rifles at medium to long range. Jamil
initially read this as a close-combat weapon,
believing that "if he kept his distance, he wouldn't
be hit." But this assumption was quickly
overturned, putting him in a tight spot on one
occasion.
 Some units instead carry a standard beam rifle.

 Its sturdy, beam-resistant armor kept it from going

throughout the unit. However, it has a weakness in

targeted; once Garrod discovered this, Croudas
began falling one after another.
 Units piloted by regular soldiers are painted

177.DSCR:
A type of unmanned mobile suit known as a Bit
Mobile Suit, controlled via brainwaves transmitted
from a Gundam equipped with the Flash System.
Because it corresponds to a Gundam, it is called a G

the moon. Armed with a beam bazooka capable of
downing even a Crouda in a single shot, and
possessing maneuverability on par with Gundam-type
units, it served as the defense system for a
microwave transmission facility.

178.DSCR:
The state of the Impulse Gundam, one of ZAFT's
new-generation high-performance 'Second Stage
Series' units, when equipped with the Force
Silhouette.
 Notable features of the Impulse Gundam include the
'Deuterion Beam Transmission System,' which allows
remote energy supply from a mother ship, the 'Core
Splendor mechanism,' in which the cockpit morphs
into a small fighter craft, and the 'Silhouette
System,' which allows the pilot to switch between
three types of weapon units to suit the battle
situation.
 Of the Impulse Gundam's three configurations, this
one boasts especially superior mobility and is
capable of independent flight even within the
atmosphere, making it the most frequently used.

179.DSCR:
The state of the Impulse Gundam, one of ZAFT's
new-generation high-performance 'Second Stage
Series' units, when equipped with the Sword
Silhouette.
 Specialized for close combat, its greatest weapon,
the massive anti-ship sword Excalibur, can be split
apart and dual-wielded, or its hilts joined together
to be wielded like a naginata. When necessary, it
can also make use of long-range weapons such as a
beam rifle.

Keeper of Unity' (one who bears the peace of ZAFT).

with the high-mobility Blaze Wizard unit. The Zaku
Phantom was mainly a commander-use mobile suit, and
unlike standard units, it also mounted a shield on
its right shoulder and featured a blade antenna on
its head for enhanced communication and command
capabilities. The Blaze Wizard is equipment that
increases mobility through thrusters placed in
various locations and boosts firepower through its
built-in missile pods. In the series, it was used
by Athrun to support the debris removal operations
at Junius Seven. Despite being a mass-production
type, it fought on equal or better terms against
stolen Gundams.

185.DSCR:
Ray Za Burrel's personal Blaze ZAKU Phantom.
 Colored white to match Ray's pilot suit, it was
nicknamed "the little white monk" by Neo.
 Though a highly versatile unit capable of operating
from space to underwater, it cannot sustain long
flights within the atmosphere, and in naval battles
it was used almost exclusively for interception from
the deck of the Minerva.
185.DSC2:
Ray Za Burrel's personal Blaze ZAKU Phantom.
 Colored white to match Ray's pilot suit, it was

 Though a highly versatile unit capable of

186.DSCR:
Dearka Elsman's personal Blaze ZAKU Phantom.
 Unlike standard units, it is colored black. Until
now, Dearka had operated machines in their stock
colors - the Gunner ZAKU Warrior he first piloted
was green, and his beloved Buster Gundam from the
previous war was white-beige. This therefore marks
the first time he has had a unit painted in his
personal color.
186.DSC2:
Dearka Elsman's personal Blaze ZAKU Phantom.
 Unlike standard units, it is colored black. Until
now, Dearka had operated machines in their stock
colors - the Gunner ZAKU Warrior he first piloted
was green, and his beloved Buster Gundam from the
previous war was white-beige. This therefore marks
the first time he has had a unit painted in his
personal color.

187.DSCR:
A unit developed by ZAFT with an emphasis on
anti-mobile-suit combat. It once lost a competitive
trial against the ZAKU and was rejected, but its
performance was later reevaluated, leading to it
entering mass production.
 Specialized for close combat, the arm-mounted shock
whip known as the 'Slayer Whip' can be used in
various ways beyond restraining enemy mobile suits -
it can also scramble electronic equipment or deal
direct damage to a pilot.
 The name GOUF is an acronym for 'Guardian Of Unity
Forerunner' (a pioneer who guards unity).
187.DSC2:
A unit developed by ZAFT with an emphasis on
anti-mobile-suit combat. It once lost a
competitive trial against the ZAKU and was
rejected, but its performance was later
reevaluated, leading to it entering mass
production.
 Specialized for close combat, the arm-mounted

suits - it can also scramble electronic equipment
or deal direct damage to a pilot.
 The name GOUF is an acronym for 'Guardian Of
Unity Forerunner' (a pioneer who guards unity).

188.DSCR:
Heine Westenfluss's personal GOUF Ignited.
 Like the ZAKU he had piloted just before this, it
has been repainted in his personal color, orange.
 In the battle at the Dardanelles Strait, combined
with Heine's skill, it shot down numerous
Murasames. It overwhelmed the Gaia Gundam from
start to finish as well, but had its right arm
severed by the Freedom Gundam, losing its combat
capability.
188.DSC2:
This is a GOUF Ignited custom unit for Heine
Westenfluss. Like the Zaku Heine had been piloting
until just before, it has been repainted in his
personal color of orange. In the battle at the
Dardanelles Strait, combined with Heine's skill, it
shot down numerous Murasames. It also consistently
overwhelmed the Gaia Gundam, but after its right arm
was severed by the Freedom Gundam, it lost its
combat capability and was bisected from behind by
the Gaia Gundam's beam blade.

189.DSCR:
Yzak Joule's personal GOUF Ignited.
 Its white-and-blue color scheme, distinct from
standard units, calls to mind his former machine,
the Duel Gundam.
 It is a unit well suited to Yzak's preference for
close combat.
189.DSC2:
Yzak Joule's personal GOUF Ignited.
 Its white-and-blue color scheme, distinct from
standard units, calls to mind his former machine,
the Duel Gundam.
 It is a unit well suited to Yzak's preference for
close combat.

190.DSCR:
An improved version of the GuAIZ, ZAFT's mainstay
mobile suit during the previous war.
 While there are no major changes in appearance, it
has been fitted with a rail gun at the waist, and
its shield, thrusters, and backpack have all been
improved, resulting in an overall boost in
performance.
 The R stands for 'Reinforce.'
190.DSC2:
This is the GuAIZ R, an improved version of the
GuAIZ, ZAFT's main mobile suit from the previous
war. Although its appearance has no major changes,
it is equipped with a rail gun on its waist, and its
shield, thrusters, and backpack have all been
improved. As a result, its overall performance has
been enhanced. The 'R' stands for 'Reinforce.' Its
base performance is not low, but because no pilot
above the level of an ordinary soldier ever boarded
it, it saw no particularly notable achievements.
Even when Sean and Dale, pilots belonging to the
Minerva, sortied in them, they were quickly shot
down by the Chaos Gundam.

191.DSCR:
A specially modified version of the GINN High
Maneuver Type, a mass-production mobile suit
developed by ZAFT during the previous war.
 It was used by a terrorist attempting to drop
Junius Seven onto Earth, interfering with the
demolition operation. Because its pilot was a
veteran soldier, its movements rivaled even the
latest models despite being an old machine. Dearka,
who witnessed it firsthand, was thoroughly
outmaneuvered and left in awe.
191.DSC2:
This is a Jin High Maneuver Type 2, a specially
modified version of the high-mobility type of the
Jin, a mass-production mobile suit developed by ZAFT
during the previous war. It was used by terrorists
attempting to drop Junius Seven to Earth, to
obstruct the debris removal work. Thanks to the
veteran pilot, its movements rivaled even the latest
models despite being an old machine. Dearka, who
witnessed it, was toyed with and impressed.
However, through the coordination of Yzak and the
others, who were even more skilled, their numbers
were gradually reduced, and the last unit was
slammed into Junius Seven and shattered.

192.DSCR:
A mobile suit developed by ZAFT based on
operational data from the DINN.
 With the ability to morph into a mobile armor form
that boosts aerial capability, a head shape designed
with air resistance in mind, and an arsenal made up
entirely of ranged weapons, it is a unit specialized
for aerial combat.
192.DSC2:
A mobile suit developed by ZAFT based on
operational data from the DINN.
 With the ability to morph into a mobile armor
form that boosts aerial capability, a head shape
designed with air resistance in mind, and an
arsenal made up entirely of ranged weapons, it is
a unit specialized for aerial combat.

193.DSCR:
A mass-production mobile suit developed by
improving the Earth Alliance Forces' Strike Dagger.
 It inherits the Strike Dagger's greatest feature,
the 'Striker Pack' weapon-swapping system. This
allows it to achieve high versatility by switching
between packs such as the Jet Striker Pack, which
enables atmospheric flight, and the Doppelhorn Pack
for long-range attacks, depending on the situation.
 A differently colored variant, the Dark Dagger L,
also exists.
193.DSC2:
A mass-production mobile suit developed by
improving the Earth Alliance Forces' Strike
Dagger.
 It inherits the Strike Dagger's greatest feature,
the 'Striker Pack' weapon-swapping system. This
allows it to achieve high versatility by switching
between packs such as the Jet Striker Pack, which
enables atmospheric flight, and the Doppelhorn
Pack for long-range attacks, depending on the
