72.DSCR:
A special member of Blue Fixer's
Special Task Force, and the pilot
of the New Pulsarvern and
Baldios.
 Because he is an alien, he was at
first suspected of being a spy and
met with strong resistance within
the base. But through his own
actions he gradually won the
crew's trust, and his outstanding
piloting skill and knowledge of
subspace mechanics eventually
earned him the position of
Baldios's main pilot.
 He holds firmly to the belief
that whatever he judges to be
right must be carried out, and he
will rush to the aid of comrades
or loved ones in danger even at
the cost of violating orders. But
that conviction is a double-edged
sword that can also become a
liability - as shown when he was
prepared to kill Marie, the news
director of World Broadcasting, to
protect Baldios's secret when she
tried to uncover the truth about
the Blue Fixer base.
 At heart, though, he is a
pure-hearted young man who
secretly loves Earth's beauty even
more than Earth's own people do.
Precisely because of this, his
determination to defeat Gattler is
fierce, and his anger toward
Aldebaron, which seeks to engulf
Earth in war, burns like a raging
fire within him.
 He seems to be hopeless when it
comes to romance: when Jamie
invited him to a concert, he
showed up at the meeting place
with Raita and Oliver in tow, an
oblivious response that hurt her
feelings.
 Though he and Aphrodia remain
enemies, their exchanges through
battle seem to have struck a chord
somewhere in his heart.
72.DSC2:
Marin Reigan is a special member
of Blue Fixer's special combat
unit and the pilot of New
Palsaverne and Baldios. As an
alien, he was initially suspected
of being a spy and faced strong
hostility within the base.
However, through his actions he
gradually won trust, and with his
superior piloting skill and
knowledge of subspace mechanics,
he was finally made the main pilot
of Baldios. He is a man of
conviction who always carries out
what he believes is right, and he
will rush to the aid of comrades
and loved ones in crisis even at
the cost of disobeying orders.
But that conviction is a
double-edged sword that can also
become a liability. This was
revealed when he was willing to
kill Marie, the news bureau chief
of the world broadcast, to protect
the secret of Baldios when she
tried to investigate the Blue
Fixer base. In truth, however, he
is a pure-hearted young man who
loves the beauty of the Earth more
than Earthlings themselves. For
that very reason, his obsession
with defeating Gattler is fierce,
and his anger toward Aldebaron,
who would engulf the Earth in war,
burns like a raging fire within
his heart. He seems oblivious in
matters of love: when Jamie
invited him to a concert, he
showed up at the meeting place
with Raita and Oliver in tow,
hurting her feelings with such a
careless response. Though he was
opposed to Aphrodia, their
exchanges through battle touched a
chord in his heart. In time, his
heart was drawn toward her, but
the war would claim Aphrodia's
life. In the unaired final
episode of the TV series, after
parting from Gattler as they
departed for a new star, he
returned alone to Earth, where he
was greeted by the phantoms of
Aphrodia and Raita. In the
theatrical version, after
descending to a Earth polluted by
radiation, he cradled the lifeless
Aphrodia in his arms and walked
toward the lighthouse where the
two had apparently first met.

73.DSCR:
A corporal in Blue Fixer's
Special Task Force and pilot of
the Baldy Prize. Twenty-two years
old.
 Born in the slums, he was placed
in a care facility together with
his younger sister Emily after
their parents separated when he
was ten. He volunteered for the
Blue Fixer Youth Corps at twelve,
and it was there that he met
Raita, who has been his best
friend ever since.
 Cheerful and quick to show his
feelings, he has the temperament
of a delinquent who won't back
down from anything he can't
stand. When he was captured by
Aldebaron and nearly turned into a
spy with a mind control device, he
cut himself with a knife rather
than lose himself, holding on to
his sanity through sheer
resistance. Having survived a
poor and rough childhood, he also
exploded with anger at the World
Federation's use of force to put
down rioters when Aldebaron's
destruction of Earth's crops
caused a food shortage, and
personally led an assault on the
Federation's warehouses.
 Yet he is by no means a crude
man: he keeps a Bible close at
hand as his constant companion,
and he has quietly continued to
carry a torch for Jamie, hinting
at an innocent side beneath the
surface.
73.DSC2:
Oliver Jack is a corporal in Blue
Fixer's special combat unit and
the pilot of Baldiprize. He is
22 years old. Born in a slum,
his parents separated when he was
ten, so he and his younger sister
Emily were placed in an
institution. He volunteered for
the Blue Fixer Boys' Corps at age
twelve, and Raita, whom he met
there, has been his close friend
ever since. He is cheerful and
wears his emotions on his sleeve,
with a delinquent streak, and he
will resist to the end anything he
cannot stomach. When captured by
Aldebaron and nearly turned into a
spy through a mind-control device,
he resisted by cutting himself
with a knife to stay sane. Having
survived a poor and turbulent
boyhood, when Aldebaron withered
the Earth's crops and caused food
shortages, he erupted in anger at
the World Federation's methods of
suppressing rioters by force, and
led an attack on the Federation's
warehouses himself. Yet he is by
no means a crude person: he keeps
a Bible at hand as his treasured
companion and secretly harbors
feelings for Jamie, revealing a
pure side. When Aldebaron's plan
to destroy humanity brought a
great flood upon the Earth, he
trembled with frustration at being
unable to save Emily and her
family, and wept alone over her
letter.

74.DSCR:
A sergeant in Blue Fixer's
Special Task Force and pilot of
the Caterranger. Twenty-one years
old. He also works as a part-time
night-school instructor at the
military academy.
 He hails from Little Japan, a
facility built at point M-29 on
the moon, and is the sole survivor
of a spaceship accident that wiped
out all its other residents. He
was raised afterward in a care
facility, enlisted in the Blue
Fixer Youth Corps at eleven, and
went on through the military
academy before joining the Blue
Fixer forces.
 A stubborn man of simple, sturdy
virtue and deep feeling. He
refuses to let others take on
dangerous missions in his place,
and is himself the brave sort who
volunteers first.
 When Marin first joined the unit,
Raita did not trust him at all,
and their exchanges often
escalated from verbal spats into
outright fistfights. But as they
weathered life-and-death
situations together, Raita came to
feel Marin's resolve firsthand and
grew to trust him completely.
74.DSC2:
Raita Hokuto is a sergeant in
Blue Fixer's special combat unit
and the pilot of the Catallenger.
He is 21 years old and also
serves as a part-time instructor
at the military academy's night
school. He is from the facility
'Little Japan' built at point
M-29 on the Moon, and is the
sole survivor of a spaceship
accident that killed all aboard.
Raised afterward in a foster home,
he joined the Blue Fixer Boys'
Corps at age eleven, went through
the military academy, and was
assigned to the Blue Fixer unit.
He is a stubborn man of solid
character and deep sentiment, who
dislikes sending others on
dangerous missions and bravely
volunteers himself. When Marin
first joined the unit, Raita did
not trust him at all, and their
arguments often escalated into
fistfights. However, as they
faced death together, he came to
feel Marin's resolve firsthand and
trusted him from the bottom of his
heart. In the unaired episode
38, he went to deal with nuclear
missiles seized by the enemy,
completed the mission, but was
fatally wounded by Gattler's
attack. Despite his efforts,
Gattler, fearing Baldios, launched
the remaining nuclear missiles,
and the Earth was polluted with
radiation.

75.DSCR:
A staff member of the Applied
Physics Laboratory within Blue
Fixer's Science Development
Bureau. Eighteen years old.
 She lived alone with her mother
from a young age, but after her
mother's death she was raised by a
Greek family of Japanese descent.
Following her adoptive parents'
deaths she entered a care
facility, and at fifteen
volunteered for the World
Federation Forces.
 She wears her emotions plainly
and cannot bring herself to
abandon someone in trouble. She
normally works under Quinstein,
but she is an active young woman
who, depending on the mission,
willingly joins Marin and the
others in actual combat.
 Her father's identity was
unknown, but during a mission to
the Kingdom of Bard, it came to
light that the King of Bard
himself was her father.
 That she was convinced early on
that Marin could be trusted shows
just how perceptive she truly is.
Perhaps it was inevitable that, in
touching and gently unraveling his
pure but lonely heart with her
compassion, she should gradually
find herself drawn to him.
75.DSC2:
Jemmy Hoshino is an 18-year-old
member of the applied physics
research laboratory belonging to
the science development bureau of
the World Federation's Blue
Fixer. From a young age, she
lived alone with her mother, but
after her mother's death, she was
raised by a Japanese-Greek
family. After the death of her
foster parents, she entered an
institution, and at age 15
volunteered for the World
Federation military.
 Her emotional expressions are
clear and direct, and she cannot
abandon people in need. She
normally works under Quinstein,
but depending on the mission, she
is an active girl who willingly
joins Marin and the others in
actual combat.
 Her father's identity was
unknown, but during a mission to
the Bird Kingdom, the truth came
to light that the Bird King was in
fact her father.
 Her early conviction that Marin
was a trustworthy person shows
that she possesses extremely keen
sensibility. It may have been
inevitable that, through her
loving care touching his pure and
lonely heart and gradually
untangling it, she came to be
drawn to him. However, since
Marin always had his eyes on
Aphrodia, her romantic feelings
never came to fruition.

76.DSCR:
Commander-in-chief of Blue Fixer,
an independent organization under
the World Federation. Forty years
old. He formerly served as
director of the World Federation's
Far East Branch.
 He initially treated Marin as a
suspected spy, but was moved by
Marin's love for Earth and
welcomed him into Blue Fixer as a
fellow fighter.
 Owing to his position, he tends
to be excessively hard on himself
- even when word came of danger to
the wife and child he had left
behind in Japan, he suppressed his
urge to go help them and tried to
ignore it. He is also a good
leader with the fairness to speak
his mind, undeterred by rank or
position, whenever someone is
clearly in the wrong.
 He shows real concern for his
subordinates as well, such as
throwing birthday parties to
reward the hard-worked Blue Fixer
members. To his troops, he is
equal to a father as much as a
commanding officer. Away from
work, though, he is an ordinary
middle-aged man whose hobbies are
watching classic films and jogging
every morning.
76.DSC2:
Goji Tsukikage is the commander
of Blue Fixer, an independent
organ of the World Federation. He
is 40 years old and formerly
served as chief of the World
Federation Far East branch.
 Initially treating Marin as a
spy, he was moved by Marin's
feelings for Earth and welcomed
him into Blue Fixer as a comrade
in arms.
 His position tends to make him
too hard on himself - even when
news of his wife and children's
crisis in Japan arrived, he
suppressed his desire to rescue
them and tried to ignore it. He
is also a good leader with the
fairness to voice his opinions
without fear of rank or position
when someone clearly acts
wrongly.
 He also showed consideration for
his subordinates, such as holding
birthday parties to reward the
hard-working Blue Fixer members.
To the members, he is not just a
superior but almost a father
figure. Away from work, however,
he is an ordinary middle-aged man
whose hobbies are watching classic
films and jogging every morning.
 In the unaired episode 34, he
sortied in a Mini Palsaburn to
rescue Marin and the others on a
suicide mission carrying
melted-down nuclear material into
subspace from the undersea base
battle, saving both Earth and the
young people by ramming the Spirit
Gattler I together with the
nuclear material.

77.DSCR:
A scientist with Blue Fixer and
director of its Science
Development Bureau. Thirty-two
years old.
 As the leader supporting Blue
Fixer on the technical side, she
developed a range of mecha, chief
among them the Baldy Prize and
Caterranger. Most notable is her
analysis and modification of the
Pulsarvern - the pinnacle of
Planet S-1's subspace engineering
- to build Baldios, a feat of
insight and technical skill that
speaks to her extraordinary
ability and expertise as a
scientist.
 She once held a position in a
research lab at Sunbridge
University, but resigned after the
World Federation ordered a halt to
joint research she was conducting
with her mentor and lover, Nerudo,
on the grounds that it risked
being converted into a weapon.
She then volunteered for the World
Federation Forces and has devoted
herself to Earth's defense ever
since.
 A strong-willed, quiet woman, she
suppresses her emotions and throws
herself into her duty. Harsh with
herself and others alike, she shot
Nerudo without hesitation when he
misused the 'Vacuum Box,' one of
her own past research
achievements, as a weapon. Yet
her granting the final wish of her
student David, who was heading
toward certain death, shows that
she is without doubt a deeply
compassionate person underneath.
 She also has a sharp eye for
talent: among the crew members
who suspected Marin of being an
alien spy, she was the first to
recognize his knowledge of
subspace mechanics and his high
piloting skill, and requested his
cooperation as a pilot for
Baldios.
77.DSC2:
Ella Quinstein is a scientist
attached to Blue Fixer and
director of the science
development bureau. She is 32
years old.
 As a leader supporting Blue Fixer
from the technical side, she
developed various machines, led by
the Baldiprize and Catallenger.
Most notably, her concept and
technical skill in analyzing and
modifying the Palsaburn - the
culmination of subspace
engineering on Planet S-1 - to
build Baldios shows extraordinary
scientific ability and
capability.
 She previously held a post at the
Sunbridge University research
laboratory, but resigned when the
World Federation issued a
suspension order for her joint
research with her mentor and lover
Nerd, citing 'risk of military
application.' Afterward, she
volunteered for the World
Federation military and has been
devoting herself to Earth's
defense.
 She is a resolute and quiet woman
who suppresses her emotions and
devotes herself to her duties.
She is strict with both herself
and others, and did not hesitate
to shoot dead Nerd when he misused
her earlier research achievement,
the 'Vacuum Box,' as a weapon.
Yet she answered the final wish of
her student Devitt heading toward
certain death, proving without
doubt that she is truly a deeply
emotional person.
 Among members who suspected Marin
of being an alien spy, she was
also one with a sure eye, quickly
recognizing his knowledge of
subspace mechanics and high
piloting skill, and requesting his
cooperation as Baldios' pilot.
 After Commander Tsukikage's
death, she serves as acting
commander of Blue Fixer to carry
on his will. In the theatrical
version, she boarded Baldios
together with Jemmy for direct
command in the final battle at
Saturn.

78.DSCR:
A pilot candidate for Blue
Fixer's Special Task Force.
 He came to the Blue Fixer base as
second pilot of the New
Pulsarvern. His nihilistic air
and provocative manner make him
easy to misjudge, but underneath
he is a man with a burning soul
who will readily throw his life
away for a cause he believes in.
 He is Quinstein's former student
and has carried romantic feelings
for her since his school days,
though he knows they can never be
returned, which torments him.
 When Aldebaron moved the moon
Ganymede to block out the sun,
David volunteered in Marin's place
to pilot the suicide weapon Fixer
1 to destroy it. His motive was
not to protect Earth, but to
protect Quinstein alone.
 Thanks to his looks and the
manner of his death, he was a
highly popular character when the
show originally aired. In the
later theatrical film, he is given
noticeably favorable treatment,
even briefly piloting Baldios.
78.DSC2:
Devitt Wayne is a pilot candidate
for the World Federation Blue
Fixer special combat unit.
 He came to the Blue Fixer base as
the second pilot of the New
Palsaburn.
 His nihilistic air and
provocative tone easily invite
misunderstanding, but in essence
he is a hot-blooded man who would
not hesitate to throw away his
life for a goal.
 He is Quinstein's former student
and has harbored romantic feelings
for her since his school days.
However, knowing those feelings
will never be requited, he is
tormented.
 To destroy the satellite
Ganymede, which Aldebaron had
moved to block sunlight, he
volunteered to board the suicide
weapon Fixer 1 in Marin's place.
His motive was not to protect
Earth but to protect only
Quinstein, just one person.
 On the night before sortie, he
confessed his feelings to
Quinstein and had his wish to
spend the night together
accepted. When he visited her
room at the appointed time,
however, he was satisfied that she
had accepted him, and sortied
without seeing her, as if cutting
off his feelings. By the time he
headed toward Ganymede, not a
trace of regret remained in his
heart.
 His looks and manner of death
made him a character of
considerable popularity during the
original broadcast. In the later
theatrical version, he was treated
quite favorably, even boarding
Baldios albeit temporarily.

79.DSCR:
Supreme commander-in-chief of
Aldebaron. Twenty-five years
old.
 She lost her parents in a traffic
accident at thirteen and was
raised, together with her younger
brother Milan, by Gattler. She
became captain of Gattler's
personal guard at twenty-three and
rose to her current position after
the coup succeeded. She holds
strong trust and loyalty toward
Gattler, and even when a classmate
from military academy told her
that it was Gattler who had had
her parents assassinated, her
devotion never wavered.
 Her skill as a commander is
exceptional; in Gattler's stead,
she personally handles everything
from devising strategy to
directing operations on the
ground. She also has a ruthless
side, having established a
merciless code under which failure
is paid for with death, and having
lured and murdered those who stood
in the way of herself or Gattler.
Even so, many resent that she
holds the post of
commander-in-chief simply by
virtue of being the Fuhrer's
trusted right hand.
 When Marin killed her beloved
brother Milan during the raid on
the Reigan Institute, she came to
hate him intensely. Because of
this, she sometimes loses her
usual composure and is swept away
by raw emotion whenever she faces
him.
79.DSC2:
Rosa Aphrodia is the supreme
commander of Aldebaron. She is
25 years old.
 At age 13 she lost both parents
in a traffic accident, and she and
her younger brother Milan were
raised by Gattler. At 23 she
became captain of Gattler's palace
guard, and after the successful
coup she attained her present
position. She holds strong trust
and loyalty toward Gattler, and
even when a classmate from the
military academy told her that
Gattler had assassinated her
parents, her heart never wavered.
 Her ability as a commander is
exceptional, and she
single-handedly handles everything
from operational planning to
on-site command in Gattler's
place. She also established the
'merciless precept' that failure
must be atoned with death, and has
a cold side that traps and murders
those who stand in her and
Gattler's way. However, many
resent that she holds the position
of supreme commander merely as the
Fuhrer's confidante.
 When the Reigan research
institute was attacked, her
beloved younger brother Milan was
killed by Marin, and she came to
hate him fiercely. As a result,
when facing Marin she would forget
her usual composure and be swept
away by passion.
 Yet as she came into contact with
Marin's purity in battle, she
gradually began to feel something
stronger than hatred. As those
feelings swelled, her heart
wavered between her duty as
supreme commander, her reverence
for Gattler, and her love-hate
toward Marin.
 In the unaired portion of the TV
version, she was driven from
Aldebaron by Negroth's treachery,
and challenged battle alone to
exact revenge but was defeated.
In the later theatrical version,
she was taken prisoner by Blue
Fixer but escaped and vanished,
only to appear at the final battle
in the subspace fortress, where
she killed Gattler with her own
hands. And while the paths
differed, in both versions she
drew her last breath in the arms
of the Marin she loved.

80.DSCR:
Fuhrer of the Aldebaron
military. He also holds the
concurrent posts of Chairman of
the Unification Council and
Chairman of the Joint Chiefs,
making him the de facto dictator
ruling the people of Planet S-1.
Thirty-eight years old.
 Not only does he possess
exceptional ability as a soldier,
but his charisma and drive let him
win the hearts of the populace in
an instant, marking him as a
leader of considerable stature.
 On Planet S-1, he served as
captain of Emperor Torinomias
III's personal guard and
repeatedly petitioned for an
escape from the
radiation-contaminated planet.
But growing impatient with the
emperor, who deferred to the
scientists working toward
restoring the environment, he used
the Aldebaron military to carry
out the emperor's assassination.
He then pinned the blame on Marin
and had the scientists, who stood
in his way, executed.
 After the coup succeeded, he
declared an evacuation from Planet
S-1, loading the citizenry aboard
the giant battleship Algol and
carrying out a warp to a new
world. Upon finding Earth, the
first habitable planet discovered,
he decided to make it their new
homeworld and ordered an attack to
exterminate humanity.
 Though generous toward his own
people, he has a ruthless side as
well, unhesitatingly discarding
subordinates who fail him if it
serves his goals. But even this
stems from the mission he set for
himself - saving the people of
Planet S-1 - and his iron will
never wavered to the end.
 He dotes on Aphrodia, both his
subordinate and something of a
surrogate daughter, and places
immense trust in her. He has
entrusted her with full authority
over the invasion of Earth, while
he himself waits in the subspace
fortress for word of the
operation's success.
80.DSC2:
Zeo Gattler is the supreme
commander of the Aldebaron
military. He also holds the
positions of chairman of the
unified council and chairman of
the joint chiefs of staff, making
him the de facto dictator who
controls the S-1 people. He is
38 years old.
 Not only does he possess high
ability as a soldier, but his
charisma and drive allow him to
quickly win the hearts of the
people, and he is a leader of
considerable caliber.
 On planet S-1, he served as
captain of the imperial guard for
Emperor Trinomias III, and
repeatedly petitioned for escape
from the radiation-contaminated
planet. However, impatient with
the emperor, who respected the
opinions of scientists seeking to
restore the environment, he used
the Aldebaron military to carry
out the emperor's assassination.
He then framed Marin for the crime
and had the troublesome scientists
executed.
 After the success of the coup, he
declared the evacuation of S-1,
loaded the citizens aboard the
giant battleship Algol, and
carried out a warp to a new
world. When he decided to make
Earth, the first habitable planet
discovered, their new home world,
he ordered an attack to
exterminate the human race.
 He is tolerant of his allies, but
he also has a heartless side, not
hesitating to discard failed
subordinates to accomplish his
goals. But this too was for the
mission he had imposed upon
himself to save the S-1 people,
and his steel will was never bent
to the very end.
 He dotes on Aphrodia, who is both
his subordinate and like a
daughter to him, and places
immense trust in her. For this
reason, he entrusted her with full
authority over the Earth invasion,
while he himself awaited news of
the operation's success in a
subspace fortress.
 Later, however, taking over from
Aphrodia who was having difficulty
conquering Earth, he took command
of a grand scheme to annihilate
humanity by melting the polar ice
caps and submerging the land.
When the resulting rise in sea
level made Earth's geography
resemble S-1 exactly, even the
bold man could not hide his
surprise.
 In the unaired episode featuring
the Saturn decisive battle, he
lost most of the S-1 people who
had departed their home world
together. Then, leading the few
compatriots remaining in the
cryogenic area, he set off to
search for a new world.

81.DSCR:
A staff officer in the Aldebaron
military.
 Though outwardly deferential to
Gattler, he is an ambitious man
scheming to topple him from the
Fuhrer's seat and rise to the top
of Planet S-1's people should the
opportunity arise.
 He harbors a deep-seated hatred
for Aphrodia, who let his twin
brother Garo die in the
Himalayas. Using the relationship
between Earth and Planet S-1, a
secret Gattler keeps tightly
hidden, as leverage, he pulled
Aphrodia down from her post as
commander-in-chief and installed
himself in her place.
81.DSC2:
Negros is one of the staff
officers of the Aldebaron
military.
 He shows a posture of submission
to Gattler, but he is an ambitious
man who schemes to topple him from
the position of supreme commander
and stand at the apex of the S-1
people, should the opportunity
arise.
 He deeply hates Aphrodia, who
left his twin brother Gallo to die
in the Himalayas. Therefore,
using the relationship between
Earth and S-1 that Gattler kept
hidden as a shield, he dragged
Aphrodia down from her position as
commander-in-chief and took her
place.
 In the TV version, he dies in an
explosion from Harman's suicide
attack, but in the theatrical
version he was given a more
important role. In the final
battle, even with defeat certain,
he attempts to press the nuclear
missile launch button to strike
back at the Earth side. This act
incurs Gattler's wrath, and he is
killed on the spot. However,
because he fell onto the nuclear
missile launch button, the
missiles were launched. The
radiation-contaminated Earth began
to transform into a new S-1.

82.DSCR:
An Aldebaron officer who secretly
fed information about his own side
to Blue Fixer.
 He has been Marin's close friend
since childhood, having studied
together with him at UF Museion, a
university on Planet S-1.
However, a rift formed in their
friendship over a matter involving
the awarding of a degree, and
Flick disappeared from Marin's
life afterward.
 He currently serves in the
Aldebaron military, waiting for a
chance to avenge comrades executed
during Aldebaron's coup. After
obtaining the location of an
important secret factory, he
sought asylum on Earth and made
contact with Marin using the
battle mecha Silver Shark. By the
time the two reunited, the old
rift between them was gone, and
they swore together to defeat
Gattler.
82.DSC2:
Flick Kyarin is an Aldebaron
officer who secretly leaked allied
information to Blue Fixer.
 He was a childhood friend of
Marin, and the two studied
together at UF Museion, the
university of planet S-1.
However, a dispute over the
acquisition of a bachelor's degree
put a rift in his friendship with
Marin, and he disappeared from
Marin's sight thereafter.
 Now, in order to avenge the
comrades who were executed during
the Aldebaron coup, he enlisted in
the military and awaited his
chance for revenge. When he
obtained the location of an
important secret factory, he
contacted Marin, hoping to defect
to Earth. There was no longer any
discord between the two upon their
reunion, and they swore to each
other to defeat Gattler.
 However, the information itself
was a trap set by Aphrodia, and
the two were trapped in a
hyper-warped space. To save
Baldios, he came up with the idea
of using the explosion of Silver
Shark to erase the distortion, and
deliberately played the villain,
attacking Baldios. Though Marin
knew his friend's true intent, he
was left with no choice but to go
along with it, and Silver Shark
was destroyed by Marin's hand,
allowing Baldios to escape by the
skin of its teeth.

83.DSCR:
Emperor of Planet S-1.
 A gentle man by nature, he
supported the group of scientists
working to restore the
radiation-contaminated
environment.
 However, under pressure from the
military at the Supreme Council,
Gattler forced him to agree that
if the radiation filtration and
circulation system was not
completed within a set deadline,
the military would be dispatched
to another planet.
 But this was not enough to
satisfy Gattler, who secretly
plotted a coup. On the very night
the system was completed, the
emperor was assassinated in his
bedroom by Aphrodia, acting under
secret orders.

84.DSCR:
The second son of the Jin family
and main pilot of Zambot 3.
Twelve years old, a first-year
middle school student.
 A local delinquent notorious for
constant fighting and riding a
motorcycle without a license, but
at heart he is kind and cannot
bear to leave anyone in trouble.
 Using piloting knowledge learned
through sleep-learning, along with
his natural athleticism and sharp
instincts, he handles the Zambird,
Zambo Ace, and Zambot 3 as
extensions of his own body. Even
so, he grew increasingly
frustrated that the people around
him failed to understand him
despite his desperate fight
against the Gaizock. But through
witnessing the Gaizock's
escalating campaign of destruction
and merciless tactics like human
bombs, and through reconciling
with those he had clashed with, he
grew as a person.

 He is a well-known delinquent in

 With piloting skills acquired

 In the final battle, even reduced
to Zambo Ace alone, he destroyed
Gaizock and, unconscious, returned
alone to his birthplace. He awoke
in the lap of Michi amid a
cheering crowd, gazing up at a
universe where war was no more.

85.DSCR:
The eldest son of the Kamie
family and pilot of the Zambull.
Fifteen years old, a third-year
middle school student.
 He has a cynical air and look
about him, but like Kappei, he is
warmhearted underneath.
Intelligent and quick-witted, he
sometimes devised strategies that
contributed to victory. He has a
younger brother named Kazuyuki and
a younger sister named Kiiro, both
of whom look up to him as a good
older brother.
 Unlike the other Jin Family
households, his has what might be
called an overbearing 'education
mom' for a mother, one who tries
to protect only her own life and
possessions with no regard for
those around her, and Uchuta felt
a sense of guilt over this. He
once clashed with Kappei after
Kappei mocked him for it, but the
two deepened their bond through
the fighting that followed.
85.DSC2:
Kamikita Uchuta is the eldest son

school student.
 He has a cynical air and
appearance, but like Kappei, his

intellectual and quick-witted, and

by devising strategies. He has a
younger brother named Kazuyuki and
a younger sister named Kiiro, and
both look up to him as a good
older brother.
 Unlike the rest of the Kami
family, he has a mother who could
be called a 'pushy mother', and he
felt a sense of debt toward her
for trying to protect only her own
life and household possessions
without regard for the situation
around them. He clashed with
Kappei over this, but through
battle their bond deepened.
 In the final battle, caught in
Bandock's ferocious assault and
realizing that neither he nor his
machine would last much longer, he
and Keiko made a suicide charge at
the thruster nozzles to open a
path. Even facing death, he
showed a kindness that put others
before himself, apologizing to
Keiko that if he had only moved
alone, she would not have been
caught up in it. Then, amid the
rising debris, crying out Kappei's
name as if entrusting his feelings
to him, he vanished into space.

86.DSCR:
The eldest daughter of the
Kamikita family and pilot of the
Zambase. A second-year middle
school student, thirteen years old
through episode eleven.
 Her family runs a ranch in
Shinshu, and she is a beautiful,
lively, and easygoing girl whose
talents are horseback riding and
archery. She has a younger sister
named Kimiko, who is introverted
and bears no resemblance to her,
in either looks or personality.
 When she returned to her hometown
for her birthday, she, like the
other members of the Jin Family,
was resented by her old friends
for reasons that were not her
fault, and was shown to have a
vulnerable side, taking the
rejection hard. But drawing
strength from her mother's
feelings, she recovered, and her
friends came to see the truth and
reconcile with her after
witnessing her continue rescue
efforts even while wounded by
stray gunfire. This inner
strength is truly her defining
trait.

 On her birthday, when she

 During the decisive battle

girl her age calling out her
father's and mother's names.

87.DSCR:

strong will and conviction as they
face the Gaizock.
 He and Umee, a trusted advisor to

bowl as a gift in his younger days

something more between them.
 He also provides the narration

87.DSC2:

changed to the third-person
perspective, 'Well then, how will

88.DSCR:
Kappei's father. Forty-eight

 A fishing boat owner who runs Jin
Fisheries in Suruga Bay. After
Beal I was discovered, he took
command of it as its captain
during battle.
 Though strict by nature, he holds
deep love for his wife and
children, a man of the sea
overflowing with warmth and manly
spirit. Having often been away
from home for deep-sea fishing, he
knows well the value of time spent
together with family.
88.DSC2:

Though strict in character, his
love for his wife and children

away from home for deep-sea
fishing, he knew the importance of
time spent with family. His end

Red Knight Deathkaine and Blue

wife to the last.

89.DSCR:

 Serious and mild-mannered in

 Possessed of sharp insight, he

 But after witnessing the

 She was later captured by the

All that remained of her was a

Another member of Kappei's
self-proclaimed honor guard, one

 Her family was likewise caught in

responsible, she directed her

 Like Aki, she was captured by the

96.DSC2:
Michi is a member of Kappei's

she vented her anger at Kappei.
Like Aki, she was captured by

97.DSCR:
Captain of the Bandock and
commander of the Gaizock, a cyborg
whose body has been replaced
almost entirely with machinery.
 Originally from a planet on the
frontier, he became a servant of
the Gaizock god (Computer Doll
No. 8) and, on its orders,
schemes to exterminate humanity.
 Cruel by nature and fond of
slaughter, he carries out one
atrocity after another, including
the human bomb operations, while
at the same time showing a strong
interest in Earth's culture and
entertainment.
 The object of his interest
changes constantly - having a
designer tailor him outfits,
indulging in pachinko, sunbathing,
or belting out songs with a band -
producing a comical side wildly
out of balance with his
ruthlessness.
97.DSC2:
Killer the Butcher is the captain
of the Bandock and the commander
of the Gaizock forces. He is a
cyborg whose body has been almost
entirely replaced with machinery.
Originally from a frontier planet,
he became a subordinate of the
Gaizock God (Computer Doll No.
8) and, following its
instructions, plotted the
annihilation of the human race.
He has a cruel personality and
treats slaughter as a hobby,
carrying out one inhumane
operation after another, including
human bombs. At the same time, he
shows a strong interest in Earth's
culture and entertainment. His
objects of interest changed each
time - he had designers tailor
costumes for him, indulged in
pachinko, sunbathed, and even
formed a band and sang
passionately. These comical
aspects stood in stark contrast to
his ruthlessness and were seen on
many occasions. When the Kamikami
family closed in on the Bandock at
the end of the fighting, he
separated the Bandock's head and
took to the battlefield himself.
Upon receiving the Ion Cannon from
Zambot 3 and realizing his
defeat, he left behind the parting
words that 'the Kamikami family's
fight is meaningless' and crumbled
away.

A weapons officer of the
Gaizock.
 A schemer who proposes various
attacks to Butcher. He also has a
foolish streak, however - on one
occasion his hand slipped while
trying to press a missile launch
switch, setting off a human bomb
and blowing himself up.
98.DSC2:

 His large build and a face

 Confident but not much of a

100.DSCR:
The electronic brain at the core
of the Bandock, and the true body
of the Gaizock.
 It had ceased activity after
destroying the planet Vier 200
years earlier. Upon approaching
Earth's sphere, it reactivated its

100.DSC2:
Computer Doll No. 8 is the
electronic brain that serves as
the true body of the Gaizock,
residing at the core of the
Bandock. After destroying the
planet Beal 200 years ago, it
halted its activities. When it
drew near Earth's sphere, it
reactivated its program and issued
orders to Butcher to eradicate
humanity. Its true nature was an
artificial intelligence created
long ago by the Gaizock people
with the purpose of driving out
all beings with malice throughout
the universe. Even when it faced
Zambo Ace after losing the battle,
it continued to insist to Kappei
until the very end that humanity
was evil, and then it collapsed.

101.DSCR:
The pilot of Daitarn 3, known
everywhere by his nickname, 'Banjo
Haran, the Talk of the Town.' He
is 18 years old.
 Cheerful and upbeat, brimming
with humor, and never without a
joke even in a crisis, he is a man
others can rely on. That he never
comes across as smug despite his
flashy, self-assured manner is
thanks to the very human side he
lets show from time to time.
 His physical abilities are
outstanding, allowing him to hold
his own against Meganoids even
unarmed. His prowess is so great
that rumors occasionally circulate
that Banjo himself might be a
Meganoid.
 He harbors fierce hatred for the
Meganoids, and for his father, who
created them and used Banjo's
brother and mother as test
subjects. He is ruthless enough
to accept the sacrifice of his
comrades if it means destroying
the Meganoids, yet his friends
still place absolute trust and
affection in him regardless.
 Note that the 'Haran
Conglomerate,' which recurred
throughout the older Super Robot
Wars titles, is an original
setting created for the games; in
the anime itself, he is simply
established as extremely wealthy.
101.DSC2:

During the decisive battle against

Noids, Banjo listened to the

rejected it, and alone brought an
end to his feud with the Mega
Noids. Note that the 'Haran
Zaibatsu,' which frequently
appeared in the old SRW series, is
an original game setting; in the
show itself, he remains merely a
very wealthy man.

The butler in service to Banjo.

 From attending to Banjo's daily

maintaining various machines, to

flawlessly - a butler among

 Nothing is known of his
background or past history, but
his great skill and character have
earned him the complete trust of
Banjo and the others.
 He is also a first-rate marksman
- so much so, by his own account,
that people used to say, "Wyatt
Earp or Garrison?"

his own account, that people used to say, "Wyatt
Earp or Garrison?"

103.DSCR:
Banjo's assistant. Age 17.
 Originally a student at the
Interpol Academy, she met Banjo
while investigating a Meganoid
incident and has traveled with him
ever since.
 Befitting her Interpol
background, she is a cool,
dependable, and intelligent beauty
well versed in handling firearms
and piloting machinery. When it
comes to Banjo, however, she is
not above clashing with Beauty,
and it is not unusual to see her
sink to the same level as her
rival.

106.DSCR:
A Civilian boy who
single-mindedly pushes forward,
true to his own convictions. He
is 16 years old.
 He broke the 'Three-Day Law' set
down by the Innocents, which held
that any crime became void after
three days had passed, and kept
pursuing Timp, the man who killed
his parents. Along the way he met
Rag and the others, and the group
tried together to steal a Xabungle
they happened to spot. They
ultimately failed, but
circumstances afterward led him to
come aboard the Iron Gear.
 He is filled with a drive that
goes well beyond mere initiative,
and once he sets his mind on
something he pushes forward no
matter what. On the surface it
looks like nothing but
recklessness, but that very
attitude embodied the 'strong
Civilian' the Innocents had longed
for across generations. His
influence spread to others
dissatisfied with the status quo,
and he ultimately struck down
Cashim King, the root of all the
trouble.
 He is quite skilled at piloting
Walker Machines, and even taught
Blume and the others at one
point. That said, his teaching
covered only the basics - he seems
to have relied more on brute force
than fine technique to get through
most situations.
 With his round face, easygoing
manner, and rough, thoughtless
personality, he would not seem, by
ordinary standards, to be popular
with girls. And yet, perhaps
because he was unconventional in
every respect, he was quite
popular with the girls around
him.
106.DSC2:
Jiron Amos is a civilian boy who
charges forward single-mindedly,
faithful to his own convictions.
He is 16 years old. Breaking
the 'Three-Day Law' established by
the Innocent, which states that
any crime becomes void after three
days have passed, he continued to
pursue Timp, the murderer of his
parents. On the way, he met Rag
and the others, and together they
tried to steal the Xabungle they
happened to come across. Though
they ultimately failed, he
subsequently ended up boarding the
Iron Gear by circumstance. He is
full of power that cannot be
contained by merely calling him
proactive - once he sets his mind
on something, he charges through
to the end. At first glance he
seems merely reckless, but that
very attitude was the embodiment
of the 'strong civilian' that the
Innocent had longed for over
generations. That influence
spread to those dissatisfied with
the current state of affairs, and
ultimately led to the defeat of
Kasim King, the root of all evil.
He is quite skilled at piloting
Walker Machines, and he sometimes
even taught Blume and the others.
However, that instruction was only
basic level; more than excelling
at fine techniques, he more often
got through by force. With his
round face, joker demeanor, crude
and thoughtless personality, by
any ordinary standard he hardly
seems the type to be popular with
girls. Yet perhaps because he was
unconventional in every way, he
was quite popular with the girls
around him. However, when Arthur
appeared, he was suddenly driven
from that position. After the
defeat of the Innocent, he made a
manly confession, declaring he
would become the eyes of the
blinded Elche, and won her heart.
And then, together with his
comrades, and those who were not
quite so, he rode off across the
wasteland.

107.DSCR:
Captain of the Iron Gear. Age
16. Her father, the trading
merchant Carrying Cargo, died in
battle, leaving her to inherit his
position against her own wishes.
 She admires the cultural life of
the Innocents and dreams of
bringing a flowering of culture to
the surface world. She herself,
though, can hardly be called
ladylike - she is quick-tempered
and handy with a throwing knife,
more tomboy than lady. Even so,
she seems to be quite
self-conscious about her
personality deep down.
 She eventually falls for the
unconventional Jiron and finds
herself locked in rivalry with Rag
over him.
107.DSC2:
Elche Cargo is the captain of the
Iron Gear, and she is sixteen
years old. Her father, the trader
Cargo, was killed in battle, and
against her own wishes she was
forced to succeed him in his
role. She longs for the cultured
life of the Innocent and dreams of
bringing the flower of
civilization to the earth.
However, she is hardly what one
would call demure; rather, she is
quick-tempered and skilled with
throwing knives, being more of a
tomboy. Even so, she seems to be
quite self-conscious about her
personality deep down. Eventually
she falls in love with the
unconventional Jiron and begins a
rivalry with Rag over him. Yet
she is abducted by the Innocent,
who have taken notice of the
new-age civilian, and the
personality of Kashiim is
implanted into her brain. Under
mental control, Elche becomes an
enemy of the Iron Gear and stands
in Jiron's path time and again.
When she is finally rescued,
Arthur's desperate gambit of
drawing Kashiim's personality into
his own brain restores her sense
of self, and with that momentum
she becomes one of the causes that
bring an end to the era ruled by
the Innocent. After the fighting
concludes, she is troubled by the
trouble she caused everyone, and
despite having lost her sight as
an aftereffect of the battle, she
slips away from the Iron Gear
alone. But the kindness and love
of Jiron, who pursues her, touches
her and shatters her resolve to
run away.

108.DSCR:
Helmsman and mechanic of the Iron
Gear.
 A rather nagging, short-tempered
man, always shouting, his
outbursts were so much like
hysterics that people called him
'Mr. Hysterics.'
 He has a deep love for machines
and absolute confidence in his
skill at maintaining and handling
them. He has also been quietly
collecting blueprints for the
machines purchased from the
Innocents, secretly harboring the
ambition of one day building
machines with his own hands
without relying on the Innocents.

109.DSCR:
Elche's loyal servant and
bodyguard.
 He was once worked like a slave
under the corrupt Lockman Gillan,
until Elche bought his freedom.
He has sworn absolute loyalty to
her ever since.
 His basic physical abilities are
extremely high, from the
tremendous strength his muscular
frame can unleash to his
surprising nimbleness. When Elche
is in danger, his abilities power
up even further, and he displays
superhuman strength.
109.DSC2:
Fatman Big is Elche's loyal
attendant and bodyguard. He was
once forced to work like a slave
under the corrupt locksmith Giran,
until Elche bought him out. Since
then, he has sworn absolute
loyalty to her. His physical
abilities are exceptional,
including the monstrous strength
from his muscular build and his
surprising agility. When Elche
falls into crisis, these abilities
are further enhanced, allowing him
to display superhuman power.
After Elche is taken by the
Innocent, he is even more
determined to fight for her sake,
and he boards the Gear Gear alone
to rescue her. Even afterward, he
continues to interact with Elche
through every means available to
him in an effort to help her
regain her memories.

110.DSCR:
The female leader of the bandit
gang Sand Rat.
 While attacking a group of
Lockmen, she got help from Jiron,
who collapsed nearby, and the two
hit it off. Lending him a hand in
stealing his Xabungle drew her
into the affairs of the Cargo
family, and eventually her whole
team was hired on aboard the Iron
Gear.
 With a temperament, nerve, and
drive that put most men to shame,
she is skilled not only at
piloting Walker Machines but also
at commanding the Iron Gear
whenever Elche is absent.
 She falls easily for anyone who
treats her like a lady, Jiron
chief among them. She even joined
the self-styled 'Arthur Honor
Guard,' though Jiron remained her
true favorite.

111.DSCR:
A member of the bandit gang Sand
Rat. Age 15.
 A quick-draw expert and a
wisecracking cynic, he plays it
cool but is kind at heart, hiding
a passionate spirit.
 He acts as something of a
sub-leader among the members. In
truth he is in love with Rag, and
resents how attached she has
become to the newcomer Jiron - a
grudge that once drove him to

112.DSCR:
A member of the bandit gang Sand
Rat. Age 16.
 Gentle and honest, kind-hearted
yet strong, considerate and full
of compassion - a rare and
valuable presence aboard the Iron
Gear, where so many others have
fiery tempers.
 Skilled with firearms, he handles
every job imaginable: piloting
and maintaining Walker Machines,
and serving as both helmsman and
gunner aboard the Iron Gear.
Despite all this, he never once
got a moment in the spotlight - a
fact summed up perfectly by his
own line, "That's because I'm a
side character." He seems to
understand his own role perfectly
well, which may make him the most
emotionally mature person in the
entire cast.

Rat.
 She carries a little bear-shaped

 Her sharp remarks about other

cries and screams like any child

dangerous.
 In Jiron's words, she will "grow

113.DSC2:

bear-shaped pouch and serves as

and without fail. Her remarks
sharply pointing out the
psychology of others reveal her
deep insight and mature mental
age. Still, when she cries out in
moments of peril, she seems every
bit her age. According to Jiron,
she will 'grow into a fine woman
someday'.

114.DSCR:
A member of the Iron Gear crew.
Age 15.
 She was once a member of the
anti-Innocent organization 'Salt,'
but gave up on their leader
Katakam out of frustration with
his ineffectiveness, and, agreeing
with Jiron's views, ended up where
she is now.
 Her active personality suits her
for reconnaissance and
intelligence work using a small
Walker Machine called the Leg,
which she carried out
energetically.
 She and Maria have fought
together aboard a captured Doran,
and the two seem to get along well
in general, including forming the
self-styled 'Arthur Honor Guard'
together and generally having
fun.

115.DSCR:
A girl who gathered orphans
together and ran a self-sufficient
farm.
 A thoroughgoing pacifist. Taking
care of others is considered
eccentric behavior on Zora, and
Rag did in fact call her a strange
one. After meeting Jiron and
recognizing her own naivety, she
cut off her long hair as a way of
atoning for it.
 She later joined 'Salt' as an
assistant to Medic. After
reuniting with Jiron and the
others, she began taking up a gun
herself and joining the fighting.
 After Arthur's appearance, she
became a huge fan of his along
with Rag and Birin, squealing with
excitement over him like any
ordinary girl.

116.DSCR:
A wandering Civilian doctor.
 A heavy drinker, but a reliable
physician. At the outset he
treated Jiron's arm and even gave
him clothes, only to have the
payment for it stolen by Rag,
effectively leaving him stiffed
for his trouble.
 He later passed through 'Salt'
before coming aboard the Iron
Gear, where he served afterward as
Jiron's strategic advisor. He is
a man of considerable
intelligence, at times making
remarks that seem to see straight
through the Innocents'
intentions.

117.DSCR:
The Breaker who killed Jiron's
parents. He seemed at first to be
a mere drifter, but he is in fact
an agent of the Innocents, whose
job is to pit Civilians against
each other under the guise of
'trials.'
 His cunning, his skill piloting
Walker Machines, and his
quick-draw marksmanship are all
first-rate, and his manner carries
the air of a truly formidable
figure. Yet he has a slightly
bumbling side too, and provided
plenty of comic moments, such as
burning his nose on the cigar
clenched in his teeth.
 He fought Jiron again and again
as Jiron pursued him to avenge his
parents, and when it finally
seemed he had been defeated, he
once got himself out of danger by
playing dead.
117.DSC2:
Timmp Sharon is the breaker who
killed Jiron's parents. He seemed
to be a drifter, but in truth he
was an agent of the Innocent, who
instigate battles between
civilians under the guise of
trials. His cunning, his mastery
of Walker Machine piloting, and
his quick draw with a gun are all
top-notch, and his bearing carries
the air of a true big shot. Yet
there is a certain
absent-mindedness about him, and
he provided many comical moments,
such as burning his nose with the
cigar he kept in his mouth. He
fought fierce battles time and
again against Jiron, who pursued
him for revenge, and when he
finally seemed to have been
defeated at Jiron's hands, he once
managed to survive the crisis by
playing dead. In the end, he
survived to the very last, and he
was still in fine form in the
final scene.

118.DSCR:
A Breaker acting as an agent of
the Innocents.
 He was once the leader of the
Breakers employed by Carrying
Cargo, but Jiron's arrival threw
everything into chaos and cost him
his position.
 From then on he devoted himself
entirely to scheming toward two
goals: defeating Jiron, and
winning over Elche, whose
affections he continued to pursue
despite her rejection.
 When he first appeared he came
across as cool-headed and sharp,
but he grew increasingly sloppy as
time went on. By the latter half
of the story, it had become a
running gag for him to take his
failures out on his partner
Geraba.
118.DSC2:
Kid Hola is a breaker who works
as an agent of the Innocent. He
was formerly the leader of the
breakers employed by Cargo, but
the arrival of Jiron threw
everything into chaos and cost him
that position. From then on, he
constantly schemed to achieve two
goals: to defeat Jiron, and to
win the heart of Elche, who had
rejected him but whom he continued
to love. At first he gave the
impression of a calm and collected
sharp operator, but gradually his
sloppiness became more and more
apparent. In the latter half, his
trademark became taking out his
frustrations on his partner Geraba
whenever he failed. Though he had
no part to play in the final
battle, he appeared properly in
the last scene, making sure to
show that he was still going
strong.

119.DSCR:
Hora's subordinate, partner, and
little brother figure.
 Tough-looking and strong in a
fight, he is also no slouch at
piloting Walker Machines.
Surprisingly timid at heart,
though, he cannot bring himself to
defy Hora, having been beaten by
him once before.
 He once pulled off the bold feat
of infiltrating the Iron Gear by
pretending to have given up on
Hora, then kidnapping Elche. The
acting skill he showed off in the
process makes one wonder whether
he could not, in fact, stand on
his own without Hora.
119.DSC2:
Subordinate, partner, and junior
to Hora. Despite his intimidating
appearance and physical strength,
and his skill at piloting Walker
Machines, he is surprisingly timid
and cannot defy Hora, who once
defeated him. He pulled off the
bold move of infiltrating the Iron
Gear while pretending to abandon
Hora, and abducting Elche. His
acting ability on that occasion
makes one cannot help but think he
could stand on his own even
without teaming up with Hora. He
had no part in the final battle,
but his appearance at the very end
was, indeed, just like Hora.

120.DSCR:
Wife of the courier Karasu
Karasu.
 The sex appeal radiating from her
overly voluptuous figure is
intense enough to overwhelm even
Jiron, and more than a few
Breakers have fallen prey to her
deep, lingering thank-you kisses.
 When she was shot down during an
attack on the Iron Gear, her
husband, believing her dead,
launched a war of vengeance - only
to be beaten back himself.
Through this convoluted turn of
events, she ended up being the one
avenging her husband instead, and
has relentlessly pursued the Iron
Gear ever since.
120.DSC2:
Wife of the transporter Karas
Karas. Her charm, emanating from
her overly voluptuous figure, was
so powerful that even Jiron was
overwhelmed, and not a few
Breakers fell victim to the
passionate kiss she gave as a
token of gratitude. When she was
shot down during the attack on the
Iron Gear, Karas believed her dead
and launched a revenge battle, but
was instead defeated. This led to
the complicated turn of events
where she herself now sought to
avenge her husband, and thereafter
she persistently targeted the Iron
Gear. In the end, following the
advice of Elche, freed from mental
control, she resolved to live on
to find new love.

121.DSCR:
The supreme ruler of the
Innocents. Age 17. His name is
a hereditary title, not his actual
birth name.
 Betrayed by his close aide
Cashim, he was imprisoned at Yopp
Point until Jiron and the others
rescued him. He then declared to
all the Innocents that Cashim must
be overthrown.
 Innocents cannot survive for long
in the open air, and it is this
frailty, along with his innocent
nature and above all his beauty,
that has captivated Rag, Birin,
and Maria.
121.DSC2:
The supreme authority of the
Innocent. He is 17 years old.
The name is hereditary, not his
real name. Betrayed by his aide
Kashim, he was imprisoned at Yop
Point until rescued by Jiron and
the others. Afterwards, he
declared to all the Innocent that
he would overthrow Kashim. The
Innocent cannot survive long in
outside air, and his resulting
frailty, his innocent personality,
and above all his beauty made Rag,
Birin, and Maria smitten with
him. When Elche suffered from
Kashim's personality being
transplanted into her, he ordered
that it be transferred into his
own body to save her. And when he
realized he could not suppress the
Kashim within, he took his own
life. However, at the end of the
theatrical version, for some
reason he appears healthy and
lively, exciting the women
greatly.

122.DSCR:
A Newtype boy who joins the AEUG,
and the pilot of the Z Gundam. He
is 17 years old.
 Originally an ordinary, if
somewhat sensitive, high school
student on the space colony 'Green
Noa.' He has a complex about his
feminine-sounding name, Kamille,
which led him to throw himself
into more masculine hobbies like
the Homo Avis (a simple hang
glider) and karate. Perhaps
thanks to having parents who were
technical officers in the
Federation Forces, he is also well
versed in machinery himself,
skilled enough to win the Jr.
Mobile Suit tournament.
 When Jerid mocked his name and
the two came to blows, however, he
found himself at odds with the
Titans. Circumstances led him to
help Quattro steal the Gundam
Mk-II, and he ended up joining the
AEUG outright. Through combat he
awakened to his abilities as a
Newtype, and gradually rose to
become one of the AEUG's ace
pilots.
 At first he simply fought out of
resentment toward the Titans, but
through his encounters and
partings with adults like Quattro
and Amuro, and with women like
Four and Rosamia, he grew
tremendously as a person. In
time, while searching for a way to
end the war, he came to fly
through space guided by his own
will.

Rosamia. And while seeking a way

the end of the TV version, his
spirit was dragged down by
Scirocco, leaving deep wounds on
his heart. But at the end of the
theatrical version, he cast that
aside and confirmed each other's
safety with Fa.

123.DSCR:
One of the central figures who
laid the foundations of the AEUG.
His rank is captain. He is 27
years old.
 A man of many mysteries, who
wears sunglasses that hide his
true face. His true identity is
Char Aznable, the Red Comet of the
Principality of Zeon forces, who
went missing after the end of the
One Year War.
 Incidentally, Quattro is Italian
for the number '4', marking it as
the fourth name he has used -
after his birth name, Casval, his
Earth alias, Edwau, and his Zeon
alias, Char.
 At first he made use of his
outstanding mobile suit piloting
skill, fighting on the front lines
aboard the Rick Dias and the Hyaku
Shiki. But his reunion with
Amuro, along with the
assassination of Brigadier General
Blex, the AEUG's representative,
led him to step into the spotlight
as a political leader.
123.DSC2:
One of the central figures who
built the foundation of the AEUG.
His rank is captain. He is 27.

difference between the mobile
suits, his machine was wrecked.
He vanished into the explosion,

124.DSCR:
The ace pilot of Karaba. His
rank is captain. He is 24 years
old.
 A man who fought through the One
Year War in the RX-78 Gundam and
has since become something of a
legend. After the war, however,
he came to be seen as a threat and
was kept under Federation
surveillance, left to languish in
an unimportant post on Earth. By
this time he had lost nearly all
his will to fight - partly due to
the oppressive environment, but
mostly because of the trauma left
by his encounter and parting with
Lalah Sune.
 A sudden visit from Fraw, Katz,
and their family, however,
prompted him to resolve to stand
up and fight again. After
deserting and joining up with
Karaba, he began working alongside
his old rival Char and the
youthful Kamille. As the fighting
continued, he regained his old
instincts, and, piloting the Rick
Dias and later the Dijeh, became a
core fighting force for Karaba.

125.DSCR:
Captain of the AEUG cruiser
Argama. His rank is lieutenant
colonel.
 During the One Year War, though
only an officer cadet,
circumstances placed him in
command of the White Base, which
he saw through to the end of the
war. His distinguished
performance, however, made him a
figure the top brass viewed with
suspicion, and after the war he
was shunted into the unimportant
post of captain of the liaison
shuttle 'Temptation.'
 Harboring doubts about the
self-righteous methods of the
Titans, he accepted Quattro's
invitation and decided to join the
AEUG.
 Drawing on the experience he
built up during the One Year War,
his sound command has led to
numerous victories.

126.DSCR:
A bridge crewman of the Argama,
serving with the AEUG.
 A cheerful, easygoing sort. His
main duties are the ship's
navigation, communications, and
sensor tracking, and he gets along
well with Saegusa, who sits next
to him and handles much the same
role.
 In the TV version he often hung
around with Kamille as well, and
once teased him into a fight that
got him sent to detention.
126.DSC2:

127.DSCR:
A bridge crewman of the Argama.
 His main duties are the ship's
navigation and helm, and he gets
along well with Torres, who sits
next to him and handles much the
same role.
127.DSC2:
A bridge crew member of the
Argama. His main role is the
ship's navigation and steering.
He is on good terms with Torres,
whose seat is next to his and who
performs nearly the same duties.
At the end of the theatrical
version, he was still handling
navigation during the quiet
conversation in which Kamille and
Fa confirmed each other's
presence.

128.DSCR:
Once a member of the Titans, she
defected to the AEUG after
witnessing Basque's despicable
tactics firsthand. Her rank
remains lieutenant.
 Her outstanding piloting skill
was apparently valued in the AEUG
as well, and she was entrusted
with mainstay machines such as the
Rick Dias, the Gundam Mk-II, and
the Super Gundam, all of which she
handled with ease.
 She has a strong will that acts
on her own convictions, along with
the sternness of a soldier. At
the same time, she also carries a
feminine gentleness. She always
kept up a cold front toward
Henken's advances, but in truth
she does not seem to have minded
them all that much.
128.DSC2:
Originally a member of the

piloting skill was evidently

against the Titans, after Reccoa
was shot down, she exited her
immobilized mobile suit and was
struck across the body by debris
fragments from Yazan's
bombardment. Afterward,
entrusting her final words to
Kamille, who rushed to her side,
she passed away in his arms.

129.DSCR:
An officer of the Titans. Her
rank is lieutenant. She is 24
years old.
 Her mobile suit piloting skill is
high enough that she was selected
as a pilot for the Gundam Mk-II
despite being a woman.
 Amid the many Titans who hold to
an elitist, chosen-people
ideology, she is one of the few
with any real sense of decency,
and this leads her to feel disgust
at Basque's ruthless, by-any-means
tactics.
129.DSC2:

130.DSCR:
A member of the AEUG, with the
rank of ensign. She is 23 years
old.
 She lost her parents during the
One Year War and spent time taking
part in guerrilla activity in
North America. Having grown up
amid fighting, she is a brave
soldier who readily volunteers
even for spy missions with death
constantly at hand. At the same
time, though, she longed for a man
who could be a source of emotional
support.

131.DSCR:
A former member of the AEUG, now
an officer of the Titans. Her
rank is ensign.
 She sought comfort in Quattro,
but his attitude and words made
her realize she was not needed by
him, leaving her disillusioned.
While on a mission she then met
Scirocco, and, drawn to him,
defected to the Titans.
 From that point on she no longer
carried out spy work as she had
with the AEUG, devoting herself
instead to piloting the Pallas
Athene.
131.DSC2:
A former member of the AEUG, now
an officer in the Titans with the
rank of ensign. She sought solace
in Quattro, but his attitude and
words made her realize she was not
needed, and she despaired. Then

battle, she fought Emma, who was
also a turncoat but on the
opposite side. She heavily
damaged the Gundam Mk-II but had
her own mobile suit shot down, and
she perished hating men to the
very end.

132.DSCR:
A subordinate of Quattro's who
joins the AEUG. His rank is
lieutenant.
 He formerly belonged to the old
Principality of Zeon forces and
took part in the One Year War as
well. He is one of the few
veteran pilots aboard the Argama,
and a good senior figure to
Kamille.
 He is deeply trusted by Quattro,
and has at times taken command of
the mobile suit corps in his
place.
132.DSC2:
A subordinate of Quattro who

lieutenant. He had originally

Quattro placed great trust in him,

shielding Fa's Methuss.

133.DSCR:

 He formerly belonged to the old

 He and Apolly are comrades who

133.DSC2:
Roberto is a subordinate of

Group, holding the rank of
Lieutenant. He formerly served in
the Principality of Zeon and
participated in the One Year War.
He is one of the few veteran
pilots aboard the Argama and

AEUG pilots use to ascend to
space. However, in the theatrical
version, he simply disappears
without a specific death scene.
Although the possibility of
survival remains, compared to his
partner who even received a
surname, he seems to have been
rather shortchanged by the
theatrical adaptation.

134.DSCR:
Kamille's childhood friend, age
17. Her name, written in kanji,
would be 'Hanazono Rei.'
 Because she was known to be an
acquaintance of Kamille, who stole
the Gundam Mk-II, she and her
parents were captured by Basque.
After Bright rescued her, she
joined the AEUG - partly out of
defiance toward the Titans - and
volunteered as a pilot. Though
troubled by her own lack of skill,
she fought her way through the
entire Gryps War.
 She has a fussy, caretaking
personality and has long kept
after Kamille about his everyday
habits and manners. Kamille, for
his part, seems to have found her
nagging rather tiresome deep
down. Perhaps because of her
personality, she also became the
one responsible for looking after
Shinta and Kum, the children
Quattro brought aboard the
Argama.
134.DSC2:
Fa is Kamille's childhood friend

name, when written in kanji, is

skill, she fought through the

lifestyle and habits. Kamille
apparently found her nagging
inwardly tiresome. Perhaps
because of this nature, she also
became the caretaker for Shinta
and Kum, whom Quattro brought
aboard the Argama. In the
television version, because her
beloved Kamille lost his sanity in
the final battle, she later left
the battlefield to devote herself
to his care and nursing. In the
theatrical version, however, the
two finished the war with their
bodies intact, and they were seen
rejoicing over each other's
safety.

135.DSCR:
A boy soldier who joins the
AEUG.
 Having come aboard the White Base
as a refugee during the One Year
War, he was raised after the war
as the adopted son of Hayato and
Fraw. When the family visited
Amuro, however, he volunteered on
his own to join the AEUG, and
joined up with Amuro aboard the
Audomura.
 A complete change from his quiet
childhood self, he has grown into
a reckless, hot-blooded young
man. He harbors rivalry toward
Kamille, who is close to him in
age, and shows a boyish immaturity
- launching without authorization,
ignoring orders, and falling for
Sara, whom he met on the
battlefield.
135.DSC2:
Katz is a boy soldier who joins
the AEUG. During the One Year
War, because of his connection to
boarding the White Base as a
refugee, he was raised after the
war as the adopted son of Hayato
and Fraw's family. However, when
his family visited Amuro, he
volunteered on his own to join the
AEUG and rendezvoused with Amuro
aboard the Audhumla. In contrast
to his quiet childhood, he became
reckless and hot-blooded. He held
a rival consciousness toward
Kamille, who was the same age, and
sometimes sortied without
permission or ignored orders. He
fell in love with Sara, a
subordinate of Scirocco, whom he
met on the battlefield, and tried
to persuade her to leave his
side. But his words were
rejected, and worse, he ended up
killing her with his own beam. In
the final battle against the
Titans, he performed a feat of
saving Emma from a desperate
situation. However, while fleeing
from Yazan's grasp, he collided
with an asteroid and scattered his
young life in space.

136.DSCR:
An officer of the Titans, with
the rank of lieutenant. He is
24 years old.
 Highly elitist by nature, he
secretly harbors ambitions of
seizing control of the Titans.
 Selected as a pilot for the
Gundam Mk-II alongside Kacricon
and Emma, he had been enjoying
smooth sailing as a soldier's
career. His encounter with
Kamille, however, threw his fate
badly off course.
 At first he was unfamiliar with
mobile suit piloting,
crash-landing the Gundam Mk-II and
standing no chance at all against
Quattro. But fueled in part by
his personal grudge against
Kamille, he steadily improved,
gradually drawing the attention of
both Jamitov and Scirocco. He
then went through one new machine
after another - the Marasai, the
Gabthley, the Byarlant, the Baund
Doc - relentlessly pursuing
Kamille all the while.
136.DSC2:
Jerid is an officer in the Titans
with the rank of Lieutenant and is
twenty-four years old. He has a
strong sense of elitism and
harbors a hidden ambition to seize
control of the Titans. He had
been walking a smooth path as a
soldier, having been selected
along with Kacricon and Emma as
pilots of the Gundam Mk-II.
However, his fate was thrown
severely off course by his
encounter with Kamille.
Initially, he was unfamiliar with
handling mobile suits, having
crash-landed the Gundam Mk-II and
being unable to do anything
against Quattro. Yet, perhaps
driven by his personal grudge
against Kamille, he steadily
improved and gradually began to
catch the attention of Jamitov and
Scirocco. While losing close
people one after another - Lila,
Kacricon, and Mouar - he kept
switching to new machines such as
the Marasai, Gabthley, Byarlant,
and Baund Doc, relentlessly
pursuing Kamille. However, even
at the end, he was outmatched, and
after his machine was shot
through, he was swallowed by the
explosion of the Radish. What he
attempted to say at the end
remains an eternal mystery.

137.DSCR:
An officer of the Titans, with
the rank of lieutenant. He is
24 years old.
 He was selected as a pilot for
the Gundam Mk-II alongside Jerid
and Emma. He gets along well with
his colleague Jerid and the two
are nearly always together.
 Besides being a skilled mobile
suit pilot, he is also
sharp-minded, the scheming,
strategist type.
 He apparently had a girlfriend on
Earth named Amelia.
137.DSC2:
Kacricon is an officer in the
Titans with the rank of Lieutenant
and is twenty-four years old. He
was selected along with Jerid and
Emma as a pilot of the Gundam
Mk-II. He got along well with his
colleague Jerid and always acted
with him. He is not only skilled
at piloting mobile suits but is
also a keen strategist with a
sharp mind. He apparently had a
lover on Earth named Amelia, and
when his Varute was slashed open
by Kamille's Gundam Mk-II during
atmospheric entry, he shouted her
name from within the burning
wreckage, and those were his final
words.

138.DSCR:
A pilot of the Galbady Beta
assigned to the Titans cruiser
'Bosnie.' Her rank is captain.
 Despite being a woman, her
piloting skill is such that she
commands the Galbady squadron.
Blunt-spoken and combative by
nature, she made no effort to hide
her rivalry with the blatantly
elitist Jerid, dismissing him
outright as a "soft little boy."
138.DSC2:
Lila Mira Raira was a pilot of a
Galbady Beta assigned to the
Titans cruiser Bosnia, with the
rank of Lieutenant.
 Despite being a woman, she
possessed piloting skill enough to
serve as the leader of the Galbady
unit. With her blunt speech and
combative personality, she made no
effort to hide her rivalry toward
Jerid, whose elitist attitude she
dismissed by calling him a
'spoiled little boy.'
 In the battle against the AEUG as
they attempted to descend to
Jaburo, she engaged Kamille's
Gundam Mk-II. She was shot down
without being able to lay a hand
on Kamille, who had only recently
begun piloting a mobile suit.
 Unlike the TV version, where she
saw potential in Jerid to become a
fine man, her role was greatly
altered in the theatrical
version. In the battle against
Scirocco, she appeared among the
figures floating around Kamille,
but...

139.DSCR:
A member of the Titans who serves
as both captain of the Garuda and
pilot of the Asshimar. His rank
is major.
 Excellent both as a commander and
a pilot, he is deeply trusted by
his subordinates. His arrogant,
overbearing manner is simply the
expression of a confidence backed
by real ability.
 He detests the instability of
Enhanced Humans, and seems to have
found the newly assigned Rosamia
an unwelcome presence as well.
 Tasked with hunting down the
Audomura, he pursued Kamille and
the others relentlessly, time
after time.
139.DSC2:
Bran Bulltaak was a member of the
Titans who served concurrently as
the captain of the Garuda and the
pilot of an Asshimar, with the
rank of Major.
 He was excellent both as a
commander and as a pilot, and
enjoyed the strong trust of his
subordinates. His arrogant and
haughty demeanor was a reflection
of confidence backed by real
ability.
 He detested the instability of
enhanced humans and reportedly
viewed Rosamia, who had been
assigned to his unit, with
distaste.
 Tasked with the mission to
eliminate the Audhumla, he pursued
Kamille and the others on numerous
occasions.
 He fought Kamille and Quattro
simultaneously and showed his high
skill, more than holding his own
against them. In the end,
however, he was defeated by the
combined efforts of Amuro and
Kamille.

140.DSCR:
Bran's adjutant, who takes
command of the Garuda's combat
operations whenever Bran sorties.
 After Bran's death, he took over
as captain of the Garuda and tried
to avenge Bran using Four's Psycho
Gundam, though he seems to have
remained skeptical of the very
existence of Enhanced Humans.
140.DSC2:
Ben Woodder was Bran's adjutant,
and when Bran sortied, he took
command of combat operations
aboard the Garuda.
 After Bran's death, he assumed
the captaincy of the Garuda and
attempted to avenge Bran using
Four's Psycho Gundam. However, he
appeared to be skeptical of the
very existence of enhanced
humans.
 After the battle in Hong Kong, he
finally resolved to carry out a
suicide attack against the
Audhumla using a Garuda-class
ship. He issued an order for the
crew to abandon ship, but the fact
that some remained despite the
order suggests he was deeply
trusted by his subordinates.

141.DSCR:
Rosamia was a cyber-newtype
trained at the Augusta Research
Institute, holding the nominal
rank of lieutenant. She lost her
family in a colony drop during the
One Year War, and her trauma was
exploited for mental enhancement.
However, the repeated experiments
and enhancements caused her mind
to become unstable. She was
assigned to Bran's unit and fought
Kamille numerous times in her
Gaplant.
141.DSC2:
Rosamia Badam was an enhanced
human trained at the Augusta
Research Institute, with the
nominal rank of Second
Lieutenant.
 She had lost her family in the
colony drop during the One Year
War, and that trauma was exploited
to perform mental reinforcement on
her. However, the repeated
experiments and the side effects
of the enhancement left her mind
unstable.
 She was incorporated into Bran's
unit and frequently engaged
Kamille in her Gaplant.
 In the TV version, she was
implanted with false memories of
being Kamille's sister, but
ultimately suffered a mental
breakdown and died at Kamille's
hands. In the theatrical version,
however, after being shot down at
Hickory, she had no explicit death
scene and appeared as a spirit in
the finale, bearing part of the Z
Gundam's power.

142.DSCR:
Four was a cyber-newtype trained
at the Murasame Research Institute
and the pilot of the Psyco Gundam,
holding the nominal rank of
lieutenant. Ordinarily gentle and
mild-mannered, when she boarded
the Psyco Gundam she came under
the influence of its mental
control waves, transforming into a
violent personality accompanied by
intense headaches. She had lost
her memories of the past, and this
deep-seated complex bound her
tightly. The name Four was not
her real name; it merely marked
her as the fourth test subject at
the Murasame Institute. Yet she
believed the words that destroying
the Gundam Mk-II would restore her
memories, and endured her
headaches to remain in the Psyco
Gundam's cockpit. Meeting Kamille
let her touch the warmth of the
human heart, but learning that he
was the Gundam Mk-II's pilot
brought her great anguish.
142.DSC2:
Four Murasame was an enhanced
human trained at the Murasame
Research Institute and the pilot
of the Psycho Gundam, with the
nominal rank of Second
Lieutenant.
 Ordinarily gentle and
mild-mannered, when she boarded
the Psycho Gundam she came under
the influence of its mental
control waves, transforming into a
violent personality accompanied by
intense headaches.
 She had lost her memories of the
past, and that loss was a deep
complex that bound her tightly.
The name Four was not her real
name; it merely meant she was the
fourth test subject at the
Murasame Institute. Yet she
believed the words that defeating
the Gundam Mk-II would restore her
memories, and endured her
headaches to keep sitting in the
Psycho Gundam's cockpit.
 Through meeting Kamille, she came
into contact with the warmth of
the human heart, but upon learning
he was the Gundam Mk-II pilot, she
fell into anguish.
 In both the TV and theatrical
versions, she lost her life amid
the flames of war. In either
case, it was the result of
throwing herself into danger for
Kamille's sake, breaking free of
her shackles, so perhaps it was
her true wish.

143.DSCR:
Mauar was a Titans officer of
seventeen, holding the rank of
lieutenant. She met Jerid while
escaping from Jaburo, and as they
worked together she came to love
him and his abilities. She
possessed solid piloting skill
backed by calm judgment and
initiative. Scirocco recognized
her potential, but she saw him as
a danger and refused his offer.
She continued to support Jerid
unwaveringly as he burned to
defeat Kamille.
143.DSC2:
Mauer Pharao was an officer of
the Titans with the rank of junior
lieutenant. She met Jerid while
escaping from Jaburo, and as they
began to work together, she came
to love both him and his
abilities. Her piloting skill was
solid, backed by calm judgment and
decisive action. Her talent was
noticed by Scirocco, but she
refused his offer, as she saw him
as a danger. She continued to
support Jerid, who burned with the
desire to defeat Kamille, and died
protecting him from an attack by
the Z Gundam.

144.DSCR:
Yazan was a Titans officer,
initially a lieutenant and later
